Thes results showed that The acute oral LD<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> of the domestic waste decomposing microbial inoculants WU-1 was estimated to be greater than 5000 mg/kg by using of Sprague Dawley (SD) rats. The domestic waste decomposing microbial inoculants WU-1 did not produce mutagenicity to Salmonella typhimurium TA97, TA98, TA100 and TA102.

articleTitle: Study on dental implant layouts of mandibular dental defect
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: From the application of the finite element analysis in biomechanical studies, this paper studies on the biomechanical model of how to reflect the true biological model, and proposes some innovative processing: mandible model simplification, boundary conditional load and accurate assignment of mandible materials. After the finite element simulations of the layouts of implant in mandibular dental defect, the optimum program of implant distribution is obtained by contrasting the results of plans. The implants are not located in original teeth sockets in the new layout. The objective of this study is to present a novel method to make a preoperative effect of implant distribution program based on biomechanics. It is helpful to the dentists make the surgical implant programs, and help the implant abutment and supporting systems to innovate, so the method has a certain practical application value.

articleTitle: The role of osthole on the human umbilical vein endothelial cells in chronic high glucose
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Osthole is used as antiproliferation, vasorelaxation, antihepatitis, anti-inflammatory, antiaggregatory, and antiallergic effects in traditional medicine. Recently, osthole has been shown to ameliorate insulin resistance and decrease the fasting blood glucose (FBG) in high-sucrose and high-fat induced fatty liver rats. However the mechanism of its anti-diabetes is not very understood. In this work we observe the effect of osthole on the human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) in chronic high glucose. Our data showed that osthole reduced the production of intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and enhanced the the concentration of nitric oxide (NO) of cultured media in the dysfunctional vascular endothelium induced by chronic high glucose. Our current results indicated that osthole can reduce the dysfunctional vascular endothelium.

articleTitle: Study of recovery effectiveness in blunt trauma rat treated by basic fibroblast growth factor-coated magnetic nanoparticles
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To study the effects of basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF)-coated magnetic nanoparticles on the recovery in rat skeletal muscles after acute contusion. Recombinant bFGF-coated magnetic nanoparticles were produced by immunochemical coupling techniques. The acute skeletal muscle contusion was produced by heavy objects dropping devices. Subcutaneous injection or blank control were performed respectively with each group and targeted and focused at the injured site with the guidance of external magnetic fields. The muscles were sampled at day 2, 10, 17, 24 and 30 respectively after contusion, and then the muscle contractive strength and relaxation were measured and calculated. The expression of MHC-II b mRNA in rat gastrocnemius was investigated by real-time PCR assay. Magnetically nanocrystallized bFGF could significantly increase the muscle contractive strength at day 17 and day 24 in gastrocnemius after contusion. From day 2 after contusion, magnetically nanocrystallized bFGF could restore the muscle relaxation back close to the normal level. Compared with the direct injection bFGF group, BFGF-coated group more significantly increased the muscle contractive strength at day 17 (P <;0.05). BFGF-coated group was significantly different from other four groups in the expression of MHC-II b mRNA at day 2-10 after contusion (P <;0.05). Magnetically nanocrystallized bFGF could significantly enhance the contractive strength, promote the expression of MHC-II b mRNA, restore the muscle relaxation and improve more effectively the healing of injured muscles in rat acute skeletal muscle contusion.

articleTitle: The influence of cricket bowler's joint rotations on ball release speed
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The aim was to identify: first, how cricket bowlers' upper body segmental rotations influenced ball release speed; second, whether flexing forcefully the lower trunk increases ball release speed and bowling accuracy. Vicon motion capture system was used to record three dimensional kinematic data of 8 male fast bowlers under three cricket bowling conditions: sub-max condition, max condition, and max-trunk condition. The accuracy of each delivery was measured. It shows that the average ball release speeds for the max-trunk condition were faster and proximal to distal sequencing was a typical pattern. A slight decrement in accuracy was observed in the max-trunk condition. In all conditions, the upper arm rotation made the largest contribution, followed in turn by torso and thorax rotation, pelvis rotation, linear velocity of pelvis, forearm and hand rotation.

articleTitle: Comparison of coronary plaque characteristics in Xinjiang Uygur and Han ethnic groups with established coronary heart disease using 64-slice CT coronary angiography
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: This study was designed to evaluate composition, location, and severity of coronary atherosclerotic plaques with 64-slice computed tomography (CT) coronary angiography in Xingjiang Uygur and Han ethnic groups. 152 Uighur ethnic group confirmed coronary heart disease (CHD) and underwent 64-Slice CT coronary angiography were included consecutively from January 2007 to June 2010. 304 Han cases examined at the same time were enrolled as control. CT coronary angiography was used to assess plaques characteristics. There were significant differences in plaques characteristics between Uygur and Han ethnic groups, with a higher incidence, higher proportion of occurred in the left circumflex branch, severer luminal narrowing, higher proportion of obstructive plaque involved multi-branch, in Uygur ethnic group. Comparison of CHD risk factors, body mass index in Uighur was higher than that in Han. Non-invasive detection of coronary plaques using 64-Slice CT may constitute an important step in risk stratification of CHD in different ethnic groups.

articleTitle: Impact of different exercise load on expression of hippocampal neurons nNOS in rats
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Discuss the impact mechanism of different exercise load on the expression of hippocampal neurons nNOS in rats. Divided 40 Wistar male rats randomly into control group of no exercise intervention and experimental groups in which the rats were applied small, medium and large intensity exercise load respectively by swimming 15, 30 and 60 minutes everyday. After experiment for 8 weeks, the expression level of hippocampal neural n-NOS were inspected by S-P Immunohistochemical Assay (IHCA). Comparing with the control group, the positive expressions of hippocampal neurons nNOS in rats of both medium and large load group are very prominent (p <; 0.01); comparing with the small load group, both medium and large load group show significant difference (p <; 0.05 and p <; 0.01); the comparison between the medium and large load group also shows very significant difference (p <; 0.01). The expression of brain hippocampal neurons nNOS is significantly improved with the increase of exercise load.

articleTitle: The clinical effects on gingivitis complicated by porcelain fused to metal treated with “YAYI” local consperge
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To contrast observation on the clinical effects of the gingivitis complicated by porcelain fused to metal (PFM) treated with "YAYI" local consperge. 120 PFM out-patients were selected to be grouped experimental and control groups randomly, each of 60 cases. The experimental group was partially treated by "YAYI" with local spraying drug, and the control group was treated with 2% iodine glycerin placed in gingiva. Recorded the plaque index (PLI) and sulcular bleeding index (SBI). The efficient of the experimental group is 80.00%, that of the control group is 58.30%, P<;0.05. Two groups have significant differences. The effects of the experimental group is better than that of the control group. It indicates that the clinical effects is obvious using “YAYI” to treat the gingivitis after PFM.

articleTitle: A brief research about the local schoolyard injure legislation of China
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: After the announcement of schoolyard injure treatment of Chinese Education Department, the various provinces of China have issued a batch of regulations and administrative rules correspondently, which play a kind of positive role in the students' injury treatment. And it is necessary to make advanced law by integrating comprehensive experiments of different places. About the new law, it aims to establish Sports Insurance, Responsibility Identification Authority and enhance other accountability systems.

articleTitle: Experimental study on growth inhibition against colon cancer of animal model by combined application of ginsenoside Rg1 and chemotherapeutic medicine
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Observe the inhibition of Rg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> against the growth of colon cancer cell strains through dye exclusion experiment in vitro. In vivo, establish the colon cancer animal model, divide the mice bearing tumor into 6 groups randomly, i.e., Rg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> 3, 1, 0.3 mg·kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> groups, cyclophosphamide group (CTX), solvent control group, and combined administration group (CTX + Rg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>); administer drug into abdominal cavity daily for 10 days, kill the animals after stopping administration for 24h, weigh them and tumors, and calculate the tumor growth inhibition rate (%) and Coefficient of Drug Interaction (CDI). Additionally, establish the SW620 ascites tumor model, assign the animals into Rg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> 3, 1, 0.3 mg·kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> groups, 5-fluorouracil group (5-FU), solvent control group, and combined administration group (Rg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> + 5-FU) randomly, administer drug into abdominal cavity daily for 5 days, record the mouse survival days, and calculate the life extension. Rg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> can inhibit the growth of tumor significantly, and extend the survival time of mice bearing tumor; additionally, Rg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> can improve the anti-tumor effect of CTX and 5-FU.

articleTitle: Comparative study of clinical features, treatment and outcome of 1354 cases of transient tachypnea of the newborn in different gestational age
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Some complications induced by transient tachypnea of the newborn (TTN) threaten the lives of newborns, medical records of 1354 cases of TTN were analyzed in order to summary the clinical characteristics of TTN in different gestational age(GA). The cases were divided into 4 groups according to GA, including small GA preterm infants, near-term infants, term and postterm infants. Clinical characteristics of different groups were analyzed and compared, including respiratory rate of admission, chest radiograph changes, the incidence of complications and respiratory support, duration of hospitalization and outcome. The study showed that there was significant difference between term and preterm infants in the chest X-ray changes (P<;0.05), the small gestational age in preterm infants had typical chest X-ray changes. Also, pneumonia as a complications was significantly increased in the small GA preterm infants (P<;0.01). The duration of continuous positive airway pressure ventilation (CPAP) was also longer in small GA preterm infants than the other groups (P <;0.05), and the median duration of hospitalization was significant difference in different GA, which suggested that the smaller the GA, the longer the duration of hospitalization. So we should pay more attention to respiratory support for TTN in preterm infants.

articleTitle: Impact of amino acid substitutions in domain 5 of high molecular weight kininogen on suppression of breast cancer cells invasion
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Domain 5 (D5) of high molecular weight kininogen represent significant anti-invasion properties towards tumor cells, and His-Gly-Lys (HGK) in D5 is the core motif for inhibition of invasion. In an attempt to identify the core amino acid of HGK in the process of tumor invasion, PCR-mediated site-directed mutagenesis technology was use to generate 3 mutant constructs, pGEX-4T-1/D5 (H485A), pGEX-4T-1/D5 (G486A) and pGEX-4T-1/D5 (K487A). These mutants fusion protein was expressed in E. coli. We further detect the effect of natural D5H and the mutants on tumor invasion and adhesion, and the expression level intracellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) in human breast cancer cells. Our study demonstrates that Lys of HGK at 487 sit plays an important role in invasion inhibition. The results also provide a potent tool to clarify the molecular mechanisms involved in D5 invasion inhibition.

articleTitle: Protective effects of ischemic preconditioning on myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To investigate the delayed protective roles of ischemic preconditioning on myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury (MIRI) in rats and its possible mechanisms. A total number of 30 rats were randomly divided into 3 groups (n=10) including sham operated group (SHAM), ischemia reperfusion group (I/R) and delayed ischemic preconditioning group (DIPC). Several important hemodynamic parameters were continuously measured and reperfusion arrhythmia was recorded; Levels of serum MDA, cTnI and CK-MB were detected; Activities of SOD, CAT and GSH-Px in serum were also determined. Compared to I/R group, an improved cardiac hemodynamics and a decreased occurrence of reperfusion's arrhythmia were observed in DIPC group. Levels of serum MDA, cTnI and CK-MB were all decreased, and the activities of serum SOD, CAT and GSH-Px were both elevated in DIPC group. DIPC could have the protective effects on MIRI through increasing the activities of antioxidant enzymes and alleviating damages of oxygen free radials on myocardium.

articleTitle: Effects of 32P irradiation on apoptosis in rat prostate cells cultured in vitro
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To study the effects of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">32</sup>P irradiation at different doses on apoptosis in rat prostate cells cultured in vitro. Rat prostate cells was cultured in vitro, and used to establish model of radiation-inducing prostate apoptosis, the apoptosis percentages of rat prostate cells irradiated by β-ray irradiation at different doses were measured by flow cytometry (FCM) and AO detection. There were three groups in this experiment, prostate cells in the control group showed typical epithelial cell shape, there was no significant change in low dose radiation group, but in high dose irradiation group a few nucleus of prostate cells randomly shrank or smashed under fluorescence microscope, the nuclear DNA of low dose radiation group and the control group showed uniform yellow, the nucleus or cytoplasm in high dose radiation group was stained dense yellow-green, low rate of cell apoptosis occurred in the low dose radiation group & the control group, the rate of cell apoptosis in high dose radiation group significantly increased, charactered by hypodiploid peak. High dose irradiation can apparently induce apoptosis in rat prostate cells, while low dose irradiation can induce little apoptosis.

articleTitle: Application of 320-slice volume computed tomography to study the correlation between coronary plaque type and acute coronary syndrome
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Objective: To preliminarily investigate the correlation between coronary plaque type and acute coronary syndrome (ACS) using 320-slice volume computed tomography (CT). Methods: Fifty-seven patients who were suspected of having ACS and underwent CT within 30 days of onset were included in this retrospective analysis. All patients underwent 320-slice volume CT coronary image examination and were divided into four groups according to the coronary plaque components: Type I, fully calcified plaque; Type II, mixed plaque (calcification >; 50%); Type III, mixed plaque (non-calcification >; 50%); Type IV, non-calcified plaque. Results: Coronary plaques were found in 53/57 patients (93%). Of these, 16 (30.2%) had type I, nine (17.0%) had type II, 15 (28.3%) had type III and 13 (24.5%) had type IV plaques, respectively. The presence of Type II-IV non-calcified plaques was significantly associated with ACS (17/53, 32.1%, p<;0.001). Type III mixed plaques were also significantly associated with ACS (p<;0.05) whereas type II mixed plaques and type IV non-calcified plaques were not significantly associated with ACS (p>;0.05). Conclusion: 320-slice volume CT coronary image can clearly depict the components of coronary plaque. Mixed plaques with non-calcified component >; 50% are significantly associated with ACS.

articleTitle: Reasonable application in the heart and cerebrovascular diseases of Chinese medicine injection
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine injection (TCM injection) basing on the traditional Chinese medicine theory is made from the extraction of effective material of natural medicine unilateral or compound by using modern scientific techniques and methods. During the course of the experience medicine transforming into the evidence-based medicine, TCM injection must prove its efficacy and safety by evidence-based medicine so that it can be better accepted by the majority of clinicians and plays its important clinical Value. Therefore, in-depth study of TCM injection used in cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases is of great significance in rational clinical drug use.

articleTitle: Reflection on the progression and prognosis of vertebrobasilar dolichoectasia: A case report with vertebrobasilar ischemic attack, hemorrhage, and brain infarction
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The diagnosis of vertebrobasilar dolichoectasia (VBD) has become easier since the development of non-invasive clinical imaging techniques. However, the early signs of VBD are not easily recognized. In order to improve the recognition and prevention of VBD, here we report a case of VBD with a history of diabetes and hypertension, which progressed from vertebrobasilar artery insufficiency into TIA gradually within a year, resulting in brain stem hemorrhage and cerebral infarction. We discussed the rapid progression and the possible reasons of the concurrent hemorrhage and brain infarction. We find that timely diagnosis with vascular imaging is necessary. The intervention of other early risk factors such as hypertension, diabetes, smoking, and heavy drinking is important to slow the progression. the application of antiplatelet therapy should be carefully considered.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of components in the volatile oil of Saposhnikovia divaricata collected from different areas at two different harvest times
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In this paper, the primary constituents in volatile oils of Saposhinikavia divarica(S.D.) collected in different harvest times were analyzed and identyfyed. Water vapor distillation was used to extract the volatile of S.D. and GC-MS was used to analyze and identify the chemical compinents of the volatile oils. As a result, the type of chemical constitents and their contents in the sample volatile oils were significantly different. 32 of 122 compounds exsited in all samples and most of them were terpenoids and chained aliphatic. The content of volatile oil in wild S.D. collected in November were higher than that in August, whereas that in the planted S.D. was higher in August than in November. It is the first time that the differce in volatile oil content between the wild and the planted S.D. is proposed. The research provide important evidences for the future research on the pharmacology, planting, quality control, and the development and utilization on the herbal medicinal resources in Saposhnikovia divaricata.

articleTitle: Research on the systematic view of PE teaching materials design
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In order to research the teaching material's designing and compiling in the university sport theoretical teaching, elaborate the principle, method and normal form of teaching material's designing and compiling systematically base on the tystematic view, including the explicit knowledge, tacit knowledge and procedural knowledge. They consist of the knowledge community of the physical education curriculum. In the knowledge community the procedural knowledge takes the central role. The characteristic of the physical education knowledge determines the non-logic, uncertain and substitutive property of the physical education curriculum. The physical education curriculum is process-orientated and experience-orientated. The framework of constructed university sport teaching material's designing and compiling has certain theoretical guidance for the sport teaching material compiling, offers feasibility and operability in compiling practice and has important meaning for raising the quality of teaching material for university physical education.

articleTitle: Clinical analysis on orthodontics of adult and teenager
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To investigate the feasibility and clinical effects of adult orthodontics by comparing with teenager patients. From 2000 to 2008, Comparing 67 adult patients with 130 teenager patients on treatment methods, effects and stability, to analyze and discuss the feasibility and clinical effects of adult orthodontics. Adult treatment course is longer than teenager patients, the clinical effects of teenager patients is better than that of adult, but the stability of adult patients is significant better than teenager patients. So for the adult patients with malocclusion deformity if conditions were permitted, the patients had strong desires to reverse with advanced technology and efficient orthodontic materials, adult orthodontics is effective and feasible.

articleTitle: Lentinan combined radiofrequency ablation and transcatheter arterial chemoembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Take 82 liver cancer patients confirmed by pathology and diagnostic imaging into this research project. 165 tumors whose average diameter of 6.5 cm (standard deviation [SD] ± 0.7) have been detected. Then the patients were divided into four groups and received four different medical treatments for each group, which are radiofrequency ablation, transcatheter hepatic arterial chemoembolization, the combination group+lentinan treatment and RFA and TACE treatment. The combination of therapies, such as lentinan, RFA and TACE treatment is more effective in extending the average survival time, increasing tumor necrosis and reducing the relapse rate than traditional treatments. Therefore, lentinan may be beneficial for patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.

articleTitle: The variation of NF-kB p65 and ICAM-1 induced by homocysteine in the brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMECs)
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Purposes Through BMEC of cultured rats, the author studies the influence of Hcy on NF-kB p65 and its downstream regulatory factors ICAM-1 (intercellular adhesion molecule-1) after BMEC is injured. Methods Cultured BMVECs were under the intervention of both 1mmol/L Hcy and CuSO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> (4μmol/L) for 0 h, 6 h, 12 h, 18 h respectively in order to observe expressions of NF-kB p65 and ICAM-1 at different time points. Results After BMVECs were exposed to 1mmol/L Hcy, compared with 0h, the expression of ICAM-1 began to appear at 6h. The expression increased as the time was extended, with remarkable higher expression at12h (/7<;0.05) and more much higher at18h(p<;0.01). After the Hcy with the same density interfered in the BMEC, the nuclear transfer of NF-kB p65 increased remarkably (p<;0.01) and then decreased gradually at 18h (p>;0.05). Conclusions Hcy may lead to the nuclear transfer of NF-kB and induce the expression of ICAM-1.

articleTitle: The study of 32P irradiation on rat prostate cells cultured in vitro
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To study the effects of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">32</sup>P irradiation with different dose on apoptosis in rat prostate cells cultured in vitro. The prostate cells were cultured in vitro, grouped (high dose irradiation group, low dose irradiation group and control group) and irradiated with different doses of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">32</sup>P, the apoptosis of rat prostate cells were detected by flow cytometry (FCM), TUNEL and MTT after irradiation. The percentage of apoptosis in low dose irradiation group and in control group was little, which was much in high dose irradiation group(P<0.01). Compared with the control group, the viability of rat prostate cells in low dose irradiation group decreased(P<0.05), more decreased in high dose irradiation group(P<0.01). Low dose irradiation can induce little apoptosis and high dose irradiation can apparently lead to more apoptosis in rat prostate cells.

articleTitle: Role of Kozak sequence polymorphism of platelet glycoprotein Iba as a risk factor for CAD after PCI
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate the changes of homeostatic activation in patients after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and its relationship with the Kozak sequence -5T/5C gene polymorphism of platelet membrane glycoprotein I ba(GP I ba). Blood samples from 86 patients with coronary heart disease undergoing in-stent implantation were collected. The change of platelet function before and after PCI was observed. The Kozak sequence gene polymorphism of GP Iba of all 86 patients was also determined by PCR-RFLP. The patients with 5C/5C genotype, The plasma levels of GMP-140 were significantly increased 24h after PCI compared with that prior to PCI (P<; 0.01) and those in patients with 5T/5C and 5T/5T genotype (P<; 0.01). We concluded that after PCI, there is more dramatic homeostatic activation in patients with 5C/5C genotype than that in patients with 5T/5C and 5T/5T genotype. This suggests that the patients with 5C/5C genotype may be a risky group of potential acute and subacute coronary thrombosis after PCI.

articleTitle: Research of effects of aloe polysaccharides on changes in cytokines during myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury in rabbits
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To investigate the effect of AP on tumor necrosis factor, interleukin -6 and Interleukin -8 during myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury. Forty New Zealand rabbits were randomly divided into five groups(n = 8), sham group(group A), myocardial ischemia reperfusion group(group B), Complex Danshen tablets group(group C), AP low dose group(group D), AP high dose group(group E). The concentrations of serum TNF-α, IL-6, IL-8 were detected. The result shows that the level of TNF-α increased obviously in 30 minutes after myocardial ischemia and after reperfusion in groups C, D, E, but less than that in group B (P<;0.05 or P<;0.01); the level of IL-6 and IL-8 increased obviously after reperfusion in groups C, D, E, but less than that in group B (P <; 0.05). Experimental studies may arrive at the conclusion that AP can inhibit the production of serum TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-8, which can protect heart tissue during myocardial ischemia and reperfusion.

articleTitle: Heating of rat skin by high power millimeter waves
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Air Force Research Laboratory published the non-lethal Millimeter wave weapon “Active Denial System” (ADS). Because of the thermal shallow penetration induced by its high frequency, the penetration depth is always less than 1mm. Heat gathers at the skin surface, caused the strong thermal effect on the skin. We built up a transient thermal multilayer model for heating of human skin by high power millimeter waves by finite volume method (FVM) based on Pennes' bioheat transfer equation in this paper. The transient temperature distributions of the cross-section profiles were calculated, and we analyzed the calculated results and compared them with the experimental ones. The veracity and reliability of finite volume model were validated. This model provides the theoretical basis for the study of the inverse problem of Active Denial System (ADS).

articleTitle: Comparison of effects on the anti-metastasis between isoliquiritigenin and glabridin
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate the anti-metastasis effects and the inhibition of the tube-like structure formation of human umbilical vein endothelial cells ECV304 of isoliquiritigenin and glabridin. The cell survival ratio of mice melanoma cells B16F1 was measured by SRB assay, the lethality rate was tested by trypan blue exclusion test. The survival ratio of human umbilical vein endothelial cells ECV304 were measured by SRB and AO/EB assays. The migration of B16F1 cells and ECV304 cells were measured by scratch wound assay. The matrix metalloproteinase-2 (MMP-2) activity in B16F1 cells culture medium was measured by gelatin zymography and ELISA methods. The inhibition on tube-like structure formation of human umbilical vein endothelial cells ECV304 were detected on artificial basilar membrane rebuilt by matrigel. Taken together, our data suggested that isoliquiritigenin and glabridin have strong anti-metastasis activities, in the same concentration, isoliquiritigenin has stronger function.

articleTitle: The expressions of β-catenin, c-myc and cyclin D1 in thymoma induced by ionizing radiation
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Wnt / β-catenin signaling pathway play an important role in the development of tumor. Here we try to study its role in tumor through investigating the expressions of β-catenin, c-myc and cyclin D1 in thymic lymphomas of mice induced by ionizing radiation. The mouse model of thymic lymphomas induced by irradiation was made according to the Kaplan' method. The mice were killed and the thymus were removed out in 3 and 6 months. The characteristics of the thymus structure was observated by histopathology and the protein expression positions of β-catenin, c-myc and cyclin D1 were detected by immunohistochemistry. The pre-cancerous changes and lymphoma were seen in the thymus 3 and 6 months later. The ectopic expression rates of β-catenin in the nucleus and the cytoplasm of precancerous lesions and thymoma were 38.5% (5/13) and 53.0% (9/17). The positive expression rate of c-myc and cyclinD1 in precancerous lesions was respectively 46.2% (6/13) and 30.8% (4/13). Their positive expression rate in lymphoma was 64.7% (11/17) and 41.2% (7/17). These results indicate that wnt signaling pathway involved in the occurrence of thymoma induced by irradiation.

articleTitle: Pharmacokinetics and tissue distribution study of schisandrin in mice by liquid chromatography
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: A HPLC method was developed to determine the concentration of schisandrin in plasma and tissues of mouse. The separation was obtained on a C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sub> column with a mobile phase of methanol: water (58:42, v/v), UV detector was monitored at 250 nm. The established method was successfully used to the research of pharmacokinetics and tissue distribution of schisandrin after intragastric administration of a 15 mg/kg dose to mice. The results of pharmacokinetic study indicate that schisandrin is quickly absorbed and eliminated. Tissue distribution research shows that liver is the major distribution tissue of schisandrin, which is beneficial to the treatment of hepatic disease.

articleTitle: Research on graduates' psychological intervention and counseling
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: University graduates can generally treat employment correctly in a positive, peaceful attitude towards a variety of problems in choosing a career. They always show a smooth and calm attitude. Of course, there are few graduate students feeling dysphoric during the graduation, and there are even someone making extreme behavior which affects the students themselves, their families, others and the society. The general view is that graduates' psychological problems of the employment include setbacks psychology, group psychology, jealousy, shyness, blind comparisons of psychological, inferiority complex, psychological dependence, and other psychologies, such as noticing affordable, the psychology of reaping where one has not sown, and overemphasize self-worth, etc. Analysing the reason of various psychologies and taking different psychological interventions for different groups are a problem which needs to be solved for the workers who are engaged in psychological research.

articleTitle: Comparison of finite element analysis of the first molar in two different rehabilitaition systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The objective of this study is to analyze the differences between split post-crown rehabilitation system and split post-core-crown rehabilitation system. Stress distributions of the models in different rehabilitation systems could be obtained through reverse engineering, virtual surgery and three-dimensional finite element analysis. Results showed that strong stress concentration appeared at the contact position between the post and the root canal in the post-crown rehabilitation system, while strong stress concentration of the adhesive appeared between the crown and the post in the post-crown rehabilitation system.

articleTitle: Experimental research on the influence of family sports upon pupils' health subtitle as needed
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: As a beneficial complement to school sports, family sports play a critical role in the healthy development of pupils; particularly, based upon the examination oriented education system currently prevailing, family sports, as an important section in family education, should be properly concerned and focused on. This passage has, through experimental method, analyzed and researched the influence of family sports upon pupils' health. Results of the research show that family sports would not only relatively completely improve pupils' physical contour and structure, strengthen the muscle force and increase the physical quality, but also would effectively improve the cardio-pulmonary function and enhance the bodily aerobic capacity of pupils. It would be beneficial for pupils' health by carrying out family sports well.

articleTitle: Investigation into injury effects and related mechanisms of advanced glycation end-products on cortical neurons
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Recent studies showed that advanced glycosylation end-products (AGEs) is toxic to central neuron system. However, the precise molecular mechanism of such toxicity has not yet been fully clarified. In the present study, we determined the injury effect of AGEs on cortical neurons cells. In vitro functional analysis using the ultraviolet spectrophotometer method revealed that AGEs increased the concentration of hydroxyl radical and malondialdehyde (MDA) in a dose-dependent way, and the effect was largely blocked by AGEs antibody (Ab-RAGE). Confocal laser microscopy showed that AGEs induced apoptosis of cultured neurons cells by its receptor(RAGE). These results indicated that increasing of hydroxyl radical and MDA levels, as well as inducing apoptosis are major mechanisms of AGEs mediated central neuron injury.

articleTitle: The variance analysis of clinical pathway in children with bronchopneumonia
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The objective of this article is to summarize and analyze the variance of clinical pathway in children with bronchopneumonia and come to a rectification in order to reduce variance cases. The objects are children with bronchopneumonia from April 2010 to April 2011 in our hospital. We made a statistic about the number of variance cases and variance reasons and got the results as below: (1) there were 46 cases into the pathway totally in the first 5 months. And 12 of them developed variance (26.1%) among which plus-variance accounts for 83.3%. Then we adjusted the standard for the averaged length of stay (ALS) from 7~14 days to 5~10 days. After that, there were 121 cases into the pathway. And 42 of them developed variance (34.7%); (2) the causes for variance include: the rapid recovery (31.9%), secondary infection (26.2%), severe condition (23.8%), accompanied by other diseases (11.9%) and applications by patients' parents (7.1%). So we draw the conclusions: (1) it is reasonable to make 5~10 days as the standard for ALS for children with bronchopneumonia in our hospital; (2) taking precautions against hospital infection would decrease variance rate effectively.

articleTitle: Protective effects of gypenosides on PC12 cell injury induced by oxidative stress
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In this study, the protective effects of gypenosides (GP) on PC12 cell injury induced by H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> was studied. Flow cytometry was used to detect the cell apoptosis, and the flow cytometry and Western blotting were used to measure Bcl-2 and Bax expressions. In addition, Effects of GP on LDH, SOD and MDA contents were observed. The results showed that GP could ameliorate PC12 cell injury induced by H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, reduce LDH release out of the cells, elevate SOD content and lower MDA content in PC12 supernatant, and increase the ratio of Bcl-2 to Bax. These indicate that GP can produce a protective effect on PC12 cell injury induced by H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, promote the body to eliminate oxygen free radicals to improve the peroxidation damage, and exerts its protective effect on the nervous cells through an antiapoptotic mechanism and regulating Bcl-2 and Bax expressions at the transcription and translation of them.

articleTitle: Relaxation effect of total flavonoids from peanut hull on rat thoracic aorta
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Objective: To explore the vasoactive effect of total flavonoids from peanut hull (TFPH) on rat thoracic aortas and its potential mechanism. Methods: The tension of thoracic aortic rings isolated from male Sprague-Dawley rat was measured in the organ bath system. Results: 1. TFPH (20-640 mg/l) concentration-dependently induced vasorelaxation (P <; 0.01 vs. control) in aortas previously contracted by KCl or phenylephrine (PE) regardless of endothelium. 2. The EC50 (80 mg/l) concentration of TFPH reduced Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>-induced contraction (P <; 0.01 vs. control) in endothelium-denuded aortas preincubated with KCl or PE. Conclusion: The vasodilatation induced by total flavonoids from peanut hull may involve the inhibition of vascular smooth muscular voltage- and receptor-dependent Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> channels.

articleTitle: Selection of surgical procedures and microsurgical techniques for one-stage hypospadias repair
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To evaluate selection of surgical procedures and microsurgical techniques for one-stage hypospadias repair. 269 cases were treated with microsurgical techniques and different method of urethroplasty. 93 cases were treated for the first time and 76 cases were return visit. The average volume of blood was 30 ml and the mean operation time was 100 minutes. There was no case of infection or necrosis of forming urethra. Penis straightened well and urinary meatus was at the normal position. Postoperative complications were urinary fistula and urethral stricture. 7 cases of urethral stricture happened in the operation of Duckett. 4 cases were cured by dilation and 2 cases were cured by discission and underwent another operation. 1 case was cured by urethral bracket. Urinary fistula could happen in all the operations. The total number was 38 cases. Hypospadias should be operated on an earlier age. With microsurgery, selection fitable surgical procedures, more experience and better techniques, we can get satisfied results.

articleTitle: Effect of nitric oxide synthase inhibitors on the changes of hemodynamic parameters and aortic tension induced by septic shock in rats
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In this study, we investigated the effect of three types of nitric oxide synthase inhibitors on the changes of hemodynamic parameters and thoracic aorta tension induced by septic shock in rats. We established the septic shock model rats by Cecal ligation and puncture (CLP), and nitric oxide synthase inhibitors (L-NAME, AMG and 7-NI) were injected after CLP. Mean arterial blood pressure (MABP), and ventricular dynamic parameters (heart rate, left ventricular developed pressure, maximal rise/fall velocity of ventricular pressure) were monitored. Isolated thoracic rings were mounted on an organ bath and the tension of the vessel was recorded. Results shown that after using L-NAME, AMG and 7-NI the mortality decreased to 50.0%, 37.5%, and 42.1%; MABP and ventricular dynamic parameters were decreased. The three types of nitric oxide synthase inhibitors can improve the hemodynamic parameters and vasoconstriction responsiveness of endothelium-denuded aorta of septic shock rats.

articleTitle: A novel biclustering with parallel genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: A novel biclustering algorithm is proposed in this paper, which can be used to cluster gene expression data. One of the contributions of this paper is a novel and effective residue function of the biclustering algorithm. Furthermore, the parallel genetic algorithm is firstly used to the algorithm of the biclustering for gene expression data. This method can avoid local convergence in the optimal algorithm mostly. The Yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae cell cycle gene expression profiles from the Spellman's data to bicluster are used to test the performance of new algorithm. And we compared our algorithm with traditional genetic algorithm in biclustering. The results reveal that novel proposed algorithms could discover the interesting patterns in the gene expression profiles.

articleTitle: Research for anti-oxidative function of Korean aconite roof polysaccharide
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Polysaccharide is widely found in plants and microorganisms. The research of polysaccharide becomes one of the most active research areas in bioscience. In this study, the anti-oxidation experimental model was established and the elimination of the ultra oxygen anion and DPPH free radical was studied. Our results suggest that korean aconite roof polysaccharide has enormously cleared ability to the ultra oxygen anion and DPPH free radical. Korean aconite roof polysaccharides can be used as a natural anti-oxidation for human cardiovascular disease treatment and preventive health care.

articleTitle: Health status and leisure sports participation of off-farm worker in Hebei province
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: As to the lack of policy guidance and support in rural off-farm workers' spirit civilization construction, specially their physical exercise activities, the current situation of Hebei rural off-farm workers participate in leisure sports exercise is investigated and studied. And the suggestion of promoting rural off-farm workers participate in physical exercise is obtained, that is, improving facilities, creating better physical exercise atmosphere, at the same time, changing rural off-farm workers' wrong idea of “physical work can replace sports activities”, and making them realize the sports exercise is good and participate in physical exercise positively, which facilitates the rural off-farm workers' physical and mental health essentially.

articleTitle: Insulin allergy in a diabetic patient: Potential factor to increase malignancy incidence
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a universal disease, and insulin is essential to control patients' blood glucose level. In some clinical cases, the diabetic patients suffer from insulin allergy, and even some of them fall into allergic shock and death. In order to analyze the potential influence of insulin allergy on systematic organs, here we report a 64-year-old patient with type 2 diabetes mellitus and administrated by insulin injection. After 3 to 4 months of insulin therapy, rashes and itching presented on the patient's generalized skin; renal carcinoma was discovered after 1 year. The results showed that the patient appeared allergy to insulin and phenol and meta-cresol inside the insulin injection may be sensibiligen. In conclusion, phenol and meta-cresol are accumulated during long-term use of insulin in patients with diabetes and may initiate occurrence of carcinoma. Clinical investigation about carcinogenicity of preservative should be performed on a large scale, and insulin injection without preservative need to be produced and applied for patients with diabetes.

articleTitle: Resection of advanced tongue cancer and reconstruction using free rectus abdominis musculocutaneous flap through extraoral approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To report the method of resection of advanced tongue cancer and reconstruction using free rectus abdominis musculocutaneous flap through extraoral approach and analyze its clinic effect. Selected six patients with advanced tongue carcinoma underwent reconstruction of total tongue and mouth floor after resection of cancer and neck dissection between 2006 and 2009. All of the operations were performed with preservation of intact mandible by way of submandible and submentum. The outcomes were evaluated. Flap survival rate was 100%. The shapes of all reconstructive tongue and mouth floor were satisfactory. The functional results in terms of speech, good swallowing and mastication were attained in 5 cases. The patients were followed up for 12 to 30 months. There was no local recurrence and metastasis. The free rectus abdominal musculocutaneous flap is a large, simple, reliable flap, which is preferred for reconstruction of defects of tongue and mouth floor after removal of advanced tongue cancer.

articleTitle: On construction of the model of excellent men volleyball players' leaping abilities
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Taking 22 Chinese Taibei men volleyball players as the subjects, we have tested 16 physical quality indexes related to the players' leaping abilities. A “0-1 program” is used to filter the tested figures according to such indexes and the selected ones will be examined by multiple regression analysis to establish the regression model. It has been tested that this model is of statistical significance. Based on this model and the standard deviation of 0.5 for the grading standards, the average number for the starting point, we work out the theoretical model concerning the development of the excellent players' leaping abilities and the main physical quality indexes, which is extremely helpful in developing the players' leaping abilities.

articleTitle: Acetabulum morphology in osteoarthritis secondary to Crowe II developmental dysplasia of the hip, a CT study
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Using computed tomography (CT) we studied the morphology of 15 patients with osteoarthritis secondary to developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH). All the patients were unilateral as Crowe II DDH. From the CT scanning, we measured acetabular depths and widths, anterior and posterior rim depths, thickness of the acetabular wall in both sides, for a statistical analysis. Statistically, there are no deficiencies in acetabular wall thickness and anterior and posterior rim depths of DDH, comparing to the opposite normal sides. While the acetabular depths and widths in the affected sides are different to the normal sides. These results suggest that surgeon should remodel the true actabulum depending on both anterior and posterior rims to obtain the proper coverage for the acetabular component, and choose suitable size and reliable location for the acetabular component with the help of CT.

articleTitle: Observation of the curative effect of two different doses somatostatin on 116 cases of esophagogastric variceal bleeding caused by cirrhosis
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Objective: Investigate the clinical effect of two different doses somatostatin on esophagogastric variceal bleeding caused by cirrhosis. Method: The patients of 116 cases of esophagogastric variceal bleeding were divided into two groups randomly. The intravenous drip at 250 μg /h was performed on 59 cases in normal dose group constantly after slowly intravenous injections of 250 μg initial dose, while the intravenous drip at 200 μg /h was performed on 57 cases in small dose group as control group constantly after slowly intravenous injections of 200 μg initial dose. Observe the treatment effectiveness of the two groups, the incidence rate of rehaemorrhagia and the changing conditions of the side effect. Result: There is no statistical difference for treatment effectiveness, the incidence rate of rehaemorrhagia and the side effect between the somatostatin normal dose group and small dose control group(P>;0.05). Conclusion: Small dose of somatostatin still has better curative effect on curing esophagogastric variceal bleeding.

Author Keywords: Esophagogastric variceal bleeding caused by cirrhosis

articleTitle: An effiecient way to extract pilose antler polypeptide and evaluation its role in the immune response
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The present study is to find an efficient method for extracting pilose antler polypeptide (PAP), and the immunological function of PAP was systematically evaluated. Sephadex G-50 Molecular exclusion chromatography and CM-Sepharose Fast Flow ion exchange chromatography were used to extract PAP which is more efficient than traditional method. Spleen lymphocyte proliferation assays and cytokine IL-12 secretion assays were used to study the immunological function of PAP. The different concentrations of PAP (4.5 ug/ml, 5 ug/ml, 5.5 ug/ml and 6 ug/ml) have significantly advanced effect on the lymphocyte cell proliferation. The result indicated that PAP may have an important immunological function to improve hosts' immunity in vivo.

articleTitle: Minimally invasive treatment of urinary bladder stone
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To investigate the best minimally invasive treatment of urinary bladder stone. March 2006 ~ September 2010 China-Japan union hospital of Jilin University had treated 55 patients who had urinary bladder stones, of which 38 patients were treated by percutaneous bladder stone lithotripsy, 17 patients by transurethral bladder stone lithotripsy. All operations were completed successfully, the simple bladder stone lithotripsy consume 30~90 min, an average of 55min. No residual stones, bladder perforation, severe bleeding happened, transurethral operation consume more time, after the removal of indwelling catheter, patients who accepted transurethral operations had urethra discomfort, the operation time decided the severity of discomfort. All patients were followed up 6 months. No bladder stones recurred, urethral discomfort in patients completely disappeared. Percutaneous lithotripsy of bladder stones to avoid the operation through the urethra, bladder stones is a good minimally invasive therapy.

articleTitle: Nerve Growth Factor pretreatment promotes vasculogenesis in rats after myocardial infarction
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To investigate the effects of NGF(Nerve Growth Factor) pretreatment on density of new vessels of acute myocardial infaction in rats. 60 male adult Wistar rats were randomly classified into three groups: the control (n=20), non-NGF (n=20) and NGF(n=20) groups. The NGF group was injected NGF (0.5μg/kg) via caudal vena. Then we performed left anterior descending coronary artery(LAD) ligation, all the rats were sacrificed at 7 days postsurgery. In this study we observe the morphologic changes of myocardial pathology and the serum biochemical changes in each group, including CK-MB, LDH and CnTI; To measure the expression of CD34, VEGF and KDR/flk-1 we use immunohistology and RT-PCR. Compared with the control group and the non-NGF group, the NGF group has a significant higher density of vessel(P<;0.01). Our results indicated that NGF pretreatment can enhance the density of new vessels, promote the vasculogenesis and lessen the myocardial damage in rats.

articleTitle: Apert syndrome: A case report
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Apert syndrome is a rare congenital type I acrocephalosyndanctyly syndrome, characterized by craniosynostosis, severe syndactyly of the hands and feet, symphalangism and dysmorphic facial features. Here we reported one case of Apert syndrome and reviewed the literature. This patient presented with the clinical triad that characterized Apert syndrome: brachycephalic skull, midface hypoplasia and syndactyly of feet. Bayley infantile development scale manifested low intellectual score in this case. Rehabilitation therapies such as physical therapy, occupational therapy and speech therapy were introduced to promote the development of motor and intelligence. One and half years follow-up showed that the patient could walk independently without abnormal gait, and the intellectual condition was improved. The aim is to alert pediatricians and surgeons about the early diagnosis and appropriate treatment may improve the quality of life and the prognosis of Apert syndrome.

articleTitle: A model for hypothermic perfusion of porcine kidney in vivo: Morphologic characteristics
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In this study, we established a model of hypothermic perfusion for porcine kidney in vivo and investigated protective effect in intraoperative on porcine renal cells. 24 porcine kidneys were randomly divided into pseudo-operation group, hypothermic perfusion group and arterial occlusion group. We detected expression of Caspase-3 protein and ultrastructure in renal cells by immunohistochemistry and transmission electron microscope. Results showed the artery occlusion group could examine cell apoptosis, necrosis ever since 1 h and hypothermic perfusion group didn't change significantly. The artery occlusion group was higher than other groups on the apoptosis index and expression of Caspase-3 ever since 0.5 h. The nuclear and mitochondrial swelling in 0.5 h and nuclear pyknosis was observed in 1 h in artery occlusion groups. Cell swelling only appeared in 0.5 h, and cell nucleus and mitochondria swelling in 1 h in hypothermic perfusion group. Therefore, the model can be used to improve the quality of kidney protection in surgical operation in vivo.

articleTitle: Rapid determination of lignans in Schisandra Chinensis and Schisandra sphenanthera by micellar electrokinetic capillary chromatography
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: A simple and rapid micellar electrokinetic capillary chromatography (MEKC) method has been developed for the simultaneous determination of six lignans, schizandrin, Gomisin A, schisantherin A, deoxyschizandrin, schizandrin B and schizandrin C, in fruits of S. chinensis and S. sphenanthera. The key factors for separation and determination were studied and the best analysis conditions were obtained, in the buffer of 10 mM phosphate-37.5 mM SDS-35% v/v acetonitrile (pH 8.0) at the separation voltage of 28.0 KV and detection at 214 nm, the plant samples could be detected within 8.2 min. Analysis yielded good reproducibility (RSD between 1.19-2.28%) and good recovery (between 92.2-102.9%). The method is quick, sensitive, accurate and it could be applied to the quality control of S. chinensis and S. sphenanthera.

articleTitle: A study of evaluation system for after-sales service of armarium based on BSC and Fuzzy AHP comprehensive evaluation
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Purpose: At present, as our country lacks of uniform evaluation standard for the after-sales service, prominent contradictions between supply and demand increasing sharply. This paper builds up a evaluation system for after-sales service of armarium. Method: Set up the framework of evaluation system and refine it's subordinate indicators through Balanced Score Card, weights each indicator by Analytic Hierarchy Process, and assess the after-sales service quality using Fuzzy AHP comprehensive evaluation model. Conclusion: This System can realize the comprehensive evaluation of after-sales service of armarium, according to the result, the system also can make the optimization of the after-sales service process. Discussion: A good evaluation system should be able to promote the development of armarium according to the feedback result, and it also able to improve itself constantly, such as refining the indicators, recomputing it's weights and so forth.

articleTitle: Projection of the corpus mamillare to the dorsal thalamus in a percomorph teleost, tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The corpus mamillare in tilapia is a prominent nucleus in the inferior lobe and has been shown to receive gustatory afferents from the inferior lobe and lateral torus, and to project to the telencephalon, nucleus ventromedialis thalami, optic tectum, and nucleus posterior periventricularis. The present study also revealed that the corpus mamillare receives afferents from the corpus glomerulosum pars anterior and nucleus lateralis valvulae, and projects to the nucleus dorsomedialis thalami in additional to fiber connections of the corpus mamillare in the above-mentioned. Because the corpus glomerulosum pars anterior is known to be a visual relay nucleus, the present study suggests that the percomorph corpus mamillare may also receive visual input besides gustatory information. Projection of the corpus mamillare to the nucleus dorsomedialis thalami was confirmed by reciprocal tracer injections. Tracer injections into the corpus mamillare densely labeled terminals in the ipsilateral nucleus dorsomedialis thalami. In contrast, injections into the nucleus dorsomedialis thalami labeled neurons in the ipsilateral corpus mamillare. Therefore, we suggest that the nucleus dorsomedialis thalami is a main projection target of the corpus mamillare in percomorph teleosts.

articleTitle: Clinical significance of Ezrin expression in ultrasound-guided HCC biopsy
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Using immunohistochemical technique to detect the Ezrin expression in 36 cases tissue of HCC acquired from ultrasound-guided needle biopsy, 45 cases tissue of HCC and 12 cases of adjacent tumor tissues acquired from operation in hepatobiliary surgery. The test show that Ezrin positive rates in the ultrasound-guided and the resectional group were significant higher than the adjacent tumor tissues. Ezrin positive rate in both groups were closely related with the tumor size and PVTT. Ezrin positive rate was correlated with histologic grade of HCC in resectional group but not in ultrasound-guided group. Therefore Ezrin play a important role in diagnosis, treatment and prognosis of HCC. Ezrin gene expression in ultrasound-guided HCC biopsy tissues has a similar meaning with it in resection HCC specimen.

articleTitle: Deferring senile effect of polysaccharides from Angelica and Astragalus on aging mice
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Angelica and Astragalus, Chinese herbal medicine, are used as immunostimulants for enriching the blood, anti-tumor and antioxidation effects. However, the synergistic mechanisms of antioxidant effect have long been the object of intensive study. We investigated the deferring senile effect of AAP on aging mice by determination of the contents of monoamine oxidase (MAO) in brain, hydroxyproline (Hyp) in skin, hydrogen peroxide (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) in serum, glutathione peroxidase (GSH-PX) and xanthine oxidase (XOD) in liver tissue and immunity organs index. The obtained results showed that AAP decreased significantly the content of MAO and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, and enhanced the concentrations of Hyp, GSH-PX and XOD in vivo. No significant differences were found when compared with those of vitamin E. Additionally, AAP could increase immunity organs index. These results demonstrated that AAP had significant deferring senile effect on the aging mice. These changes may be the important mechanisms to prevent mice from aging.

articleTitle: Investigation and research on current situation of physical training of adolescent basketball players of Ji'an City, Jiangxi Province
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Research methods adopted include documentation and questionnaire survey. Through an in-depth research on current situation of physical training of adolescent basketball players of Ji'an City, Jiangxi Province, this paper puts forward approaches and methods of physical training of adolescent basketball players for providing reference for the coach.

articleTitle: Anti-HHV-6 action of Baicalin in vitro
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Human Herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) was first isolated from peripheral blood lymphocytes of patients with various lymphoproliferative disorders, and then identified as the main pathogen of roserash and acute febrile illness of early childhood. The primary HHV-6 infection in adults is related to many diseases, such as necrotizing lymphadenitis, chronic fatigue syndrome, hepatitis and mononucleosis-like syndromes. Like most other herpes-viruses, after primary infection, HHV-6 is likely to remain latent in the host and can be reactivated in immunosuppressed states, leading to critical clinical symptoms such as interstitial pneumonitis. At present, little is known about the mechanism of latency and reactivation of HHV-6 so there is no effective specificity drug on HHV-6 infection. Therefore, it is very important to find safety and effective anti-HHV6 drugs. To study the anti-HHV-6 action of Baicalin, the human T-cell strain was used to do the anti-HHV-6 effect in vitro. The result shows that Baicalin has evident effect on cytopathic effect (CPE) caused by HHV-6 GS. This result prompts that Baicalin has therapeutical effect on infection caused by HHV-6.

articleTitle: In vivo PET imaging of diabetic encephalopathy rat model
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: It is the study about the role of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup>F-FDG PET imaging technology in differentiating diabetic encephalopathy (DE) rat model. 10 rats were injected with Streptozotocin to use as duplicate DE model rats, and 10 rats were injected with normal saline to use as control rats. The change of rat behavior was observed. HE staining was made to detect the intracerebral pathological changes in rats. In both groups, the conditions of intracerebral glucose metabolism in rats were observed in vivo through <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup>F-FDG PET imaging technology. Under PET imaging, glucose metabolism decreased in hippocampus in model group, and there were only mild neuron injury and slight glucose hypometabolism in control group. The combination of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup>F-FDG PET imaging with behavioral and pathological observation could become one of ways to determine whether the model is successful.

articleTitle: Increased histamine by thioperamide exerts its neuronal protection effect through postsynaptic H1 receptor in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy rat model
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Blocking histamine H3 receptor leads to increased histamine in the brain. The effects of H3 receptor antagonist in the rat model of neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (NHIE) and its mechanism is uncertain. In our study, we employed a NHIE model of postnatal 7 days rats and tested the brain water content, hippocampal histamine, cerebral MDA and SOD levels under the different combinations of H1, H2 and H3 antagnonists in order to investigate the effect of H3 antagonist and its mechanism in the NHIE model. H3 antagonist thioperamide decreased the brain water content and MDA and increased the hippocampal histamine and SOD level; H1 antagonist pyrilamine reversed the effects of thioperamide in the H3+H1 group, however, H2 antagonist has no significant influence on the effects of thioperamide as their combinational use. We deduce that thioperamide plays a neuronal protective role by increasing brain histamine through postsynaptic H1 receptor in the NHIE model.

articleTitle: Effects of inducers or inhibitors of autophagy and apoptosis combined with ionizing radiation on MCF-7 cells
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In order to find sensitive drugs in the radiotherapy of human breast cancer, some experiments were done to detect autophagy and apoptosis on MCF7 cells. MTT method detected cells proliferation; flow cytometry detected cells apoptosis; real-time PCR method analyzed the relative expression amounts of mRNAs. Results showed cells proliferation reduced with the extension of irradiation and apoptosis increased. The apoptosis percentage of the cells in the 4-Gy + rapamycin group increased significantly as compared with that in the 4-Gy + 3-MA and 4-Gy + z-VAD-FMK groups. The relative expressions of LC3B, beclin-1, p53 and Bax mRNA increased significantly in MCF-7 cells treated by irradiation jointing with autophagy inducer, while those of Akt1 and Bcl-2 mRNA decreased significantly. Ionizing radiation can inhibit cells proliferation and promote cells apoptosis. Ionizing radiation jointing with autophagy inducer affects not only the autophagy pathway, but also the apoptosis pathway.

articleTitle: Culture and identification of dendritic cells from mouse bone marrow in vitro
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Establish a method of cultivation and purification of dendritic cells (DCs) from mouse bone marrow in vitro to provide experimental material and establish basis for the study of immunological tolerance. BALB/c (H-2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup>) mice spleen lymphocytes and bone marrow cells were extracted under sterile conditions and cultured in RPMI 1640 medium. DCs were induced by recombinant granulocyte macrophage colony stimulating factor (GM-CSF) and interleukin (IL-4). Then, the morphology of DCs was observed under light microscopy and CD80, CD86 expression levels were detected by flow cytometry. The results showed that bone marrow cells appeared irregular and formed dendritic processes after 3 days cultured with stimulating factors in vitro which present the typical morphology of dendritic cells; Costimulatory molecules (CD80, CD86) were low expression on the cellular surface. Obtaining DCs from bone marrow cells is a promising method, which might meet further study on function, marker and anti-tumor role of DCs in vitro.

articleTitle: Induced expresssion pattern of Rab9 in CpG — Activated macrophages and construciton of Rab9 eukaryotic expression vector
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: This study is to learn the expression patterns of small Rab GTPase Rab9 in macrophages induced by CpG and construction of Rab9 eukaryotic expression vector. Rab9 expression in different murine tissues was detected by RT-PCR and Real-time PCR. RAW264.7 cells were stimulated with CpG(0.3μM) for different times, and relative mRNA expression of Rab9 was measured by RT-PCR and Quantitative-PCR. Using the cDNA of RAW264.7 cells as a template, the full-length of Rab9 was amplified and introduced into the restriction site of eukaryotic expression vector pc-DNA3.1(-)/Flag(-)B. The recombinant Rab9 vector was then verified by double restriction enzyme digestion and sequence analysis. RT-PCR and Real-time PCR results have revealed that Rab9 was expressed in the liver, lung, kidney, spleen, testicle, ileum and colon of mouse, and the highest expression of Rab9 was found in ileum and colon. After CpG stimulation, Rab9 mRNA expression in RAW 264.7 cells began to decrease at 8-12h, and then resumed slightly the expression at 24h but still lower compared with the original expression. Quantitative-PCR results verified the induced expression pattern of Rab9. Sequence analysis on the recombinant Rab9 vector has showed that the sequence of full-length Rab9 was 100% homologous with the sequence in genbank. In the mouse macrophage cells, Rab9 mRNA expression is negatively regulated by CpG. Rab9 eukaryotic expression vector was successfully constructed.

articleTitle: Quantitative determination of total alkaloid in Corydalis Ochotensis Turcz by colorimetry
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: A quantitative determination of the total alkaloid in Corydalis Ochotensis Turcz was established by acid dye colorimetry. The effects of wavelength, pH of the phosphate buffer and the quantity of acid dye were studied. Two different dyes were compared according to the yield of berberine hydrochloride. The method with bromophenol blue dye was proved to be more accurate, more stable with good reproducibility in testing experiments. So, it was fit for quantitative determination of total alkaloid in Corydalis Ochotensis Turcz.

articleTitle: Effects of EPP on place orientation and space exploration dysfunctions in mice
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Pentobarbital was used to induce the place orientation and space exploration dysfunctions. Morris water maze was used to observe mice's abilities of place orientation and space exploration. Bradford method was used for the determination of the total protein and spectrometry method was used for the detection of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) activity. Extract of Polygala tenuifolia and Poria cocos (EPP) could shorten the escape latency in place orientation test and increase numbers of mice's crossing the location where the platform had been in the space exploration test. EPP could decrease AChE activities in the brain and the serum of mice with learning and memory disorders induced by pentobarbital. EPP would improve the learning and memory abilities of mice induced by chemical drugs. The results demonstrate that EPP would improve place orientation and space exploration dysfunctions of mice and it; exerts its effects perhaps by inhibiting AChE activity to reduce acetylcholine (ACh) hydrolysis in the brain and the serum in mice.

Author Keywords: Extract of Polygala tenuifolia and Poria cocos (EPP)

articleTitle: Identification of ginsenosides Rc, Rb2, Rb3 and related malonyl-ginsenosides in panax ginseng extracts by using RRLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Ginsenosides Rc, Rb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and Rb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> were studied by using Rapid resolution liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole-time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry (RRLC-Q-TOF MS/MS). The MS/MS fragmentation pathway has been studied of this group of isomers and characteristic fragment ions have been proposed, which are helpful for the differentiation of the isomers. Ginsenosides Rc, Rb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, Rb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and related malonyl-ginsenosides were differentiated and identified in the extracts of ginseng by using RRLC-Q-TOF MS/MS, which were identified by comparing retention time of the standard compounds, the accurate mass, and the analysis of characteristic fragment ions.

articleTitle: Disposition of arsenic in saliva, blood and urine of Sprague-Dawley rats following repeated oral exposure to sodium arsenite
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Biological monitoring for arsenic(As) was usually based upon a determination of urine and blood arsenic concentration, however, saliva had been suggested as a non-invasive biological matrix for assessing exposure.
