Methods Thirty New Zealand rabbits were randomly divided into groups A1, A2, A3, A4 and C. Animals in groups A1–4 were intravenously injected (i.v.) with 5 μmol/kg, 10 μmol/kg, 20 μmol/kg and 40 μmol/kg PASP-USPIO, while animals in group C were injected (i.v.) with 0.2 mmol/kg gadolinium diethyl triamine-pentoacetic acid (Gd-DTPA), serving as a control group. Each group was subjected to T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∗</sup> Gradient Echo-Echo Planar Imaging (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∗</sup>GRE-EPI)-sequenced perfusion-weighted imaging to obtain signal intensity-time curves, which were used to calculate the regional cerebral blood volume (rCBV), the maximum signal drop percentage (SRR<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>), and Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rCBV</inf>-Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SRRma</inf>X values. Data were compared within and between groups. Results The intra-group rCBV value and SRR<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> value were significantly different between gray matter and white matter. The inter-group Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rCBV</inf> and Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SRRmax</inf> values were also significantly different. ANOVA analysis indicated that the Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rCBV</inf> and Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SRRmax</inf> values in group A4 were significantly different from those in other groups, while there were no significant differences among group A1, A2, A3 and C. Conclusion PASP-USPIO has colloid stability and can be used in normal rabbit MR brain perfusion. The optimal dosage is 10 μmol/kg.

articleTitle: Progress in the studies on effective components of Chinese medicine in the treatment of hyperlipidemia
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Currently the incidence of hyperlipidemia is significantly increasing and the age of onset is younger. Lipid regulating drugs can adjust and improve the lipid metabolism. More and more people are favor of the chemical drugs used for treating hyperlipidemia because of its rapid onset and positive efficacy. But the chemical drugs have side effects of different levels. Through the study we find that some elements of traditional Chinese medicine have positive, continuous effect, less side effects, show the unique advantages in treating hyperlipidemia and preventing the cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. The effective component of Chinese medicine of treating hyperlipidemia involves more than 30 kinds of compounds. In this paper compounds of polysaccharides, flavonoids, saponins, alkaloids, phenols, fatty acids are reviewed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the blood and genetic compatibility of coronary artery stents
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The aim of our study was to evaluate the blood and genetic compatibility of coronary artery stents. We investigated blood compatibility of the sample products by some tests including platelet aggregation test, platelet counts, The Thromboxane B2 concertration, determination of thrombin time, prothrombin time, activated partial throboplastin time and fibrinogen concertration after the samples were inserted into the common carotid artery of a rabbit; genetic compatibility was evaluated by using three in vitro tests that are Ames test, micronucleus test, as well as chromosome aberration test. The results of the these tests preliminarily showed that the coronary artery stents were biocompatible, laying a foundation for further studies and applications of the coronary artery stent.

articleTitle: Methods of weight control for rhythmic gymnastic athletes adopt L-carnitine
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: With the competition of rhythmic gymnastics athletes, rhythmic gymnastics workers in every country all general realized having an ideal heavy is one of the indispensable factors of improving rhythmic gymnastics technical value. Studies in athletes have shown that L-carnitine supplementation may foster exercise performance. In this paper the mechanism of negative energy balance principle and L-carnitine supplementary for rhythmic gymnastics athletes' weight control are presented. The results of control experiment show both the mechanism of negative energy balance principle and L-carnitine supplementary are effective to rhythmic gymnastics athletes' weight control. And the L-carnitine supplementary is more efficient. Study shows that rhythmic gymnastics athletes eat L-carnitine three times every day, 2g/d and last 4 months, the thickness of sebum would be reduced 4.71 cm, the decrease rate reached 7.5%.

articleTitle: Pharmacokinetics of pseudo-ginsenoside GQ after intravenous administration in rats
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Pseudo-ginsenoside GQ is a new semisynthetic ocotillol-type saponin with remarkable anti-myocardial ischemia activity. The purpose of this study was to characterize the pharmacokinetics of pseudo-ginsenoside GQ (PGQ) after sublingual intravenous administration in rats. Rats (n=200) were given 3.0, 12.0, 48.0 mg·kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, and were taken blood at 2, 5, 10, 20, and 40 min and 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, and 24h after drug administration. Ginsenoside Rb1 was used as the internal standard. Serum concentrations of PGQ were determined using HPLC-ELSD. By using the mean concentrations at each time point (n=6), pharmacokinetic parameters were estimated for PGQ using a 2-compartment model with the reciprocal of the predicted concentration as the weight factor. The linear relationship between AUC and the dose of PGQ was obtained in the range of 3.0-48.0 mg · kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>.

articleTitle: On how to strenthen psychological counseling for construction of harmonious campus psychological environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: With the increasingly greater stress on the study and employment for college students, their psychological problems stand out accordingly. Strengthening psychological counseling on college students in ideological and political education for college students is the innovation of the ideological and theoretical construction of our Party in universities. How to carry out the ideological and political work with epoch function according to the characteristics of our age should be the widely concerned issue for ideological and political workers. On the basis of the exact and profound understanding about the scientific connotation of psychological counseling, the necessity and urgency of the psychological counseling in the ideological and political work on college students should be fully realized. And we should carefully consider how to strengthen psychological counseling in the ideological and political work for college students from the perspective of rational thinking.

Author Keywords: ideology and politics for college students

articleTitle: HPLC-fingerprint study on medicinal Folium Fici Microcarpae of Guangxi
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: HPLC-fingerprint of Folium Fici Microcarpae of guangxi was studied in the paper. By reverse-phase high performance liquid chromatography, the herbal leaves of Ficus microcarpa taken from 10 sites in Guangxi province were analyzed. The analysis was conducted under the following conditions: an Ultimate ODS (5 μm, 4.6 mm × 250 mm) chromatographic column and acetonitrile-0.05% phosphoric acid solution were selected for gradient elution; detection wavelength was at 280 nm; flow rate at 0.5 mL/min; and analysis period of 120 min. Twelve chromatographic peaks were determined through similarity analysis under the chosen chromatographic conditions to identify the characteristic fingerprint peaks of Folium Fici Microcarpae. The method used to establish the fingerprints is deemed of good stability and reproducibility. Not only is it applicable for quality control of Folium Fici Microcarpae, but also an effective means for fundamental study of valid substances.

articleTitle: The changes of acid-sensing ion channel 1a in focal cerebral ischemic diabetes rats and neuroprotection of fasudil
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The symptoms of diabetes focal ischemia were more serious, but the concrete machanism is not very clear. For this we measure the expression of Acid - sensing ion channel 1a (ASIC1a) in ischemic cortex of diabetic rats during different time, meanwhile observe the protection of fasudil after ischemia. 72 male wistar rats were divided into 3 groups: focal ischemia, diabetes focal ischemia and fasudil interfere, ischemia 1h, 3h, 6h, 24h per group. high fat diet plus streptozotocin to model diabetic, thread cork to establish the models of focal ischemia. interfere group received 1mg/Kg fasudil injection by tail vein during half an hour after making diabetic model. The expressions of ASIC1a were detected by Western Blot. the results indicated diabetes groups were serious, ASIC1a were increasing and time-dependent (P<;0.05); After fasudil, ASIC1a decreased significantly. So the aggravated cause of diabetes ischemia maybe associate with excessive opening of ASIC1a., Fasudil is neuroprotective by inhibit the expression of ASIC1a.

articleTitle: The research for extracting effective components process of Stigma maydis and Silkworm chrysalis and their hypoglycemic effect
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To establish the method for extracting the effective components process of Stigma maydis and Silkworm chrysalis and to research the hypoglycemic effect of the diabetic mice. The extracts were taken from a certain proper proportion of Stigma maydis and Silkworm chrysalis after the pretreatment. The different doses of extracts were respectively flowed into stomach of the Kunming mice, and then we would observe the influence on the glucose tolerance of normal mice and hyperglycemia induction of alloxan, adrenaline, glucose There was no obvious influence on mice of glucose tolerance used by the extracts, whose function factor were bringing the different levels of inhibition impact on blood glucose rising of diabetes animal models caused by alloxan, adrenaline, glucose. The better hypoglycemic effect on diabetic mice model were taken by the extracts of Stigma maydis and Silkworm chrysalis.

articleTitle: One-factor analysis of variance for medical statistical data with binomial distribution
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The new method of one-factor analysis of variance for medical statistical data with binomial distribution is studied in this paper. The total probability variation of the control groups is decomposed into sample probability variation and probability variation between samples in control groups, the statistical analysis will be done to the data with binomial distribution by using one-factor analysis method. Result The result by this method is correct. The conclusion by this method is reliable.

articleTitle: Testicular torsion: Diagnosis and treatment
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To review the predisposing factors of testicular torsion, diagnosis, treatment and prognosis. There were 34 patients in China-Japan union hospital of Jilin university from Jan 2000 to Nov 2008. The clinical data of these patients were analyzed retrospectively. Orchiectomy was performed in 24 patients, orchiopexy was performed in 10 patients, 3 patients developped atrophic testis at half-a-year follow-up, 1 patient developped atrophic testis at one-year follow-up, 1 patient developped atrophic testis at one year and a half follow-up, the other 5 patients had the normal development with the same testis' size and texture as other contemporaries upon follow-up. Timely diagnosis and treatment should be given to testicular torsion with 6 hours. The best treatment is surgical exploration for patient suspected testicular torsion. If the operation is not completed in time, the results are severe: orchiectomy, testicular atrophy after orchiopexy.

articleTitle: The role of LT-β as a main cytokine involved in immunoreglution disorders from SLE
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate expression of lymphotoxin-β (LT-β) in patients with systemic lupus erythematosis (SLE) and its role in the immunoregulation disorders resulting from SLE. LT-β protein in serum of 82 SLE patients and 90 healthy people were detected with ELISA and PBLs were separated for analyses of its encoding sequence with RNA spot hybridization. The polymorphism of LT-β gene was analyzed by PCR-RFLP. The expression levels of LT-β in SLE patients were significantly higher than those in the control group (P<;0.05); those in active group was significantly higher than that in inactive group (P <;0.05). Hybridization results showed a significant difference in LT-β mRNA values between SLE patients and control groups (P<;0.05); the polymorphism of LT-β gene Xho I cleavage sites was not found in the both groups. The results suggest that LT-β is the main cytokine related to SLE, which is involved in the immunoregulation disorders resulting from SLE.

articleTitle: Effect of resveratrol on oxidative stress in kidneys of diabetic rats
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Objective: Observation the effect of resveratrol on oxidative stress in kidneys of diabetic rats. Methods: Fifty Sprague Dawley(SD) rats (male) were randomly divided into four groups: the normal rats, the diabetic rats treated with resveratrol(10mg/kg/d), the diabetic rats treated with resveratrol(20mg/kg/d) and the diabetic rats treated with resveratrol(40mg/kg/d). After 12 weeks, the levels of blood glucose, serum creatinine, 24h urinary protein, the contents of malondialdehyde(MDA), glutathione(GSH) and the activity of antioxidant enzymes total superoxide dismutase (T-SOD) in the renal tissue were measured. Results: Compared with the diabetic model group, the levels of blood glucose, serum creatinine, 24h urinary protein and MDA in the renal tissue were decreased, the activity of T-SOD and GSH in the renal tissue was increased, the renal pathologic changes was improved in resveratrol treated group. Conclusions: Resveratrol can increase the renal function and antioxidant capacity, it has protective effect on kidney of diabetic rats.

articleTitle: Effects of Geraniin in Geranium sibiricum L. on antioxidant function of S180 mice
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Objective: to investigate effects of Geraniin in Geranium sibiricum L. on antioxidant function of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">180</sub> mice. Methods: S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">180</sub> entity-tumor mice as study model were used to investigate effects of Geraniin on tumor inhibition rate and indices of immune organs of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">180</sub> mice; kits were used to determine SOD activity and T-AOC activity in red blood cells and MDA content of red blood cells in the whole blood of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">180</sub> mice. Results: Geraniin could significantly inhibit growth of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">180</sub> entity-tumor, significantly increase thymus index and spleen index, significantly increase SOD activity and T-AOC activity in red blood cells of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">180</sub> mice and significantly reduce MDA content of red blood cells in the whole blood of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">180</sub> mice. Conclusion: Geraniin could significantly inhibit the growth of entity-tumors of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">180</sub> mice and its effect mechanism was possibly associated with increase of antioxidant function of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">180</sub> entity-tumor mice.

articleTitle: Experimental observation on antihypertensive ability of total flavonoids from Jumi in spontaneously hypertensive rats
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: We observed the level of lowering blood pressure (BP) and heart rate (HR) of SHR by total falconoid from Jumi. We used SHR models, intervene them by total falconoid from Jumi, and rats were divided into SHR control groups, nifedipine control group, total falconoid high dose groups, total falconoid medium dose groups and total falconoid low dose groups. We observed the level of Bp and HR by non-invasive blood pressure. Total falconoid from Jumi significantly reduced the levels of Bp and HR when after 3 h treating by single dose test. Total falconoid from Jumi reduced the levels of them and lasted four hours and it took slower effect than nifedipine in successive administration. Effect of lowering Bp and HR among three dose groups of total falconoid wasn't significant difference. Total flavonoids from Jumi could reduce Bp and HR of SHR, and it had a better long-term effect for mild-to-moderate hypertension.

articleTitle: Protective effects of exenatide on RINm5f cell injury induced by palmitate
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In this study, in vitro cultured islet RINm5f cells were used to observe effects of exenatide on the apoptosis induced by palmitate and explore its mechanism. MTT, AO/EB bi-label assay, flow cytometry and laser confocal microscope were applied for the observation of the cell proliferation, survival rate, apoptosis rate and morphological change. The results confirmed that the survival rate of cultured rat islet RINm5f cells treated with 250 μM palmitate for 24h was lower. Compared with the control group, the survival rate was higher, the apoptosis rate was lower and died cells and necrotic cells were less in exenatide groups. These facts indicate that exenatide can promote cell proliferation and improve rat islet cell apoptosis induced by palmitate, and promoting pancreatic B cell growth, increasing B cell volume, improving and restoring B cell function should be a new strategy used for the treatment of diabetes.

articleTitle: The prognostic significance of joint detection of vascular endothelial growth factor & interleukin-12 in acute leukemia
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In order to examine the diagonostic and prognostic significance of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and interleukin-12 (IL-12) in acute leukemia (AL), we measured the serum levels of VEGF and IL-12 in 25 patients with AL at different stages. Study indicates that serum levels of VEGF are higher in the untreated and recurrent AL patients than in healthy examinees. IL-12 levels are much lower in these patients. VEGF levels are reduced and IL-12 levels are increased in completely remitted patients. A negative correlation (r = −0.96) between the VEGF and IL-12 levels is observed in the normal control group. The data implies that patients with high VEGF and low IL-12 levels have a smaller chance for complete remissions: the illness easily goes recurrent and the prognosis is unsatisfactory. Our study suggests that joint detection of VEGF and IL-12 could be employed in AL diagnosis and prognosis.

articleTitle: Effects of different temperature and humidity on the quality of Chinese yam (Rhizoma dioscoreae) during storage
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Chinese yam is easily mouldy and decayed during the process of storage and transportation because of high water content in the tissue of tubers associated with injures during or after harvesting which makes them vulnerable to micro-organisms disease. The temperature and the humidity as vital factors in the preservation were studied. Graded temperature and humidity were adopted to observe the effects on the preservation quality of Chinese yams. The results showed that room temperature (18~23 °C) combined with low humidity (RH, relative humidity 15%~20%) had good effects on maintaining the quality of Chinese yams. On day 80, indexes including PPO, MDA, TSS and firmness of yams stored at room temperature were 5.64 U/g-FW, 0.74 μ mol/L, 1.83%, 10.80×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> N/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and those of samples stored in RH 15%~20% were 2.72 U/g-FW, 0.49 μ mol/L, 1.81%, 10.59×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> N/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively, which were better than other storage condition.

articleTitle: An experimental study of Baji Quan's functions on the physical health of male college students
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Baji Quan is one of the fine boxing in the Chinese martial arts. According to research. When Baji Quan is being played, boldness and tenderness can be seen. Some movements are fast, some slow. Some are long strides, some short. Rhythmic changes can be seen. This essay is based on the experimental study of male college students in conducting the Baji Quan exercise. The study demonstrates: The intensity of the Baji Quan exercise can create a suitable load for the male college students and can promote the physical body and health of the male college students. The Baji Quan drilling can raise the breathing function and body stability function of the male college students. The Baji Quan exercise can promote the pliability of the various joints of the abdomen, lower limb strength, shoulders, body trunk, waist, pelvis etc., muscle and ligaments of the male college students.

articleTitle: Trend and risk of diagnostic medical exposure to Taiwan population
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Due to the rapid growth of diagnostic medical examination frequencies in recent years for imaging modalities such as the computed tomography and the interventional fluoroscopy, the population dose and the health risk from medical exposure are of increasing interest. The temporal trends over time for the population dose from diagnostic examinations provide data on the promotion of high standard quality assurance programs. In the present work, studies have been performed to illustrate the trends from 1997 to 2008 for the examination frequencies and effective doses of diagnostic examinations in Taiwan. The frequency data were extracted from the Taiwan Health Insurance Research Database. The average effective dose per examination was derived from hospital surveys, measured data, and published results. Estimates of the collective and per caput effective doses were made for radiography, fluoroscopy, mammography, computed tomography, interventional fluoroscopy, and nuclear medicine. Risks of cancer induction from medical exposure were also estimated.

articleTitle: Reflections on future development of high-level sports teams in Jiangxi regular institutions of higher learning
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The paper is designed to put forward several targeted suggestions in allusion to the issues appeared in routine training and administration of high-level sports teams in seven Jiangxi regular institutions of higher learning, such as lack of fund, shortage student source, the contradiction between team members' routine study and after-class training, etc.

articleTitle: The clinical applications of titanium mesh multi-point forming shaping in craniocerebral trauma patients
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Summarized the skull defect cases caused by craniocerebral trauma of our hospital in the past 5 years. To research the clinical applications of Titanium Mesh Multipoint Forming Shaping in Craniocerebral Trauma Patients. The following aspects were analyzed: the different irritation to soft tissue between different repair materials, difficulty of shaping, anesthesia and surgery time, appearance satisfaction, and postoperative complications. The surgical procedures are simple. It can greatly reduce shaping time, anesthesia time and operation time, reduce the risk of surgery, and greatly reduce the chances of postoperative infection and hydrops. The multi-point forming technology reduces the intensity of the work of Neurological Surgeons, decrease the postoperative complications. It can significantly improve the patients' quality of life; reduce the use of titanium screw to save operation costs. The multi-point forming technology in titanium mesh shaping is much better than other skull repair technology. It creates huge economic and social benefits.

articleTitle: Transurethral electroresection of tumor of ureter gap (report of 65 cases)
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To discuss whether transurethral electroresection could be used in tumors of ureter gap. 65 cases were treated with transurethral electroresection. The operation time was 5~90 minutes and the average time was 35 minutes. The average time in hospital was 8 days. Pathological examination was done as a routine for all the patients. All the patients acquired follow-up visit and time was 6 months ~24 months. Urethral stricture happened in 4 cases and they were cured by regular distension. There was no stricture or back flow of ureter gap after intravenous urography and cystography. 5 cases recurred in 7 ~13 months after the operation. Chemotherapy was used after operation. Stricture happened in 4 cases which were cured by dilation of urethra. There was no case of ureterostenoma and backstreaming of ureter. Relapses happened in 5 cases which were undergone another operation and cured.

articleTitle: Application of molecular biology techniques on the identification of Trionycis carapax
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Objective: To establish an accurate, rapid and efficient method to identify the characterization of DNA fingerprint from Trionycis carapax by using molecular biology techniques. Methods: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA)was extracted from Trionycis carapax by phenol extraction method and salting-out method respectively. The cytobchrome b (Cytb) partial gene from Trionycis carapax was amplified with PCR by designing specific primers and the PCR products were sequenced and blasted in Genbank. Results: Complete 17.3 kb mtDNA was extracted from Trionycis carapax. The Cyt b gene sequence revealed that the 362 bp segments were identical to that described in GenBank accession number AY687385. Conclusion: Molecular biology techniques can be applied to identify the characterization of DNA fingerprint from Trionycis carapax, with achieving the efforts that were rapid, efficient in addition to high specificity.

articleTitle: High-voltage electric burns: Relation between electric injury and burns on cause of death
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In this study, we report an unusual death case. A 40-year-old man was found dead in the roof terrace on the construction site. Because he touched the 10, 000 volt high-tension transmission line when he transported the steel bars and caused the burning of greasy dirt in scene. The prosecutor considered the death suspicious due to safety protection and improper rescue in the scene, that is the death due to electric or burn or both. Autopsy, the cadaver's chest-abdominal cavity was explosive open and the internal organs were revealed and carbonized. The lower limb was mutilated. In this case, there were the electrical marks and the electrical striation in the cadaver's left internal malleolus and both feet. The black soot particles weren't found in the nostrils, mouth and respiratory tract. The autopsy led to the conclusion of electrocution.

articleTitle: The elder diet investigation and analysis of elderly apartments in Shandong province
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The purpose of this paper was to know the elderly diet and nutritional status of elderly apartments in Shandong province, then give some suggestions for improvement. The method of investigation was a continuous 3-day bookkeeping meanwhile conbing the retrospection, which lasts 2 months in 45 apartments of six regions (effective 38), Shandong province. The results is as follows: the composition of diet and nutritional status are all unreasonable in elderly apartments of Shandong province, which is urgent for nutrition improvement. So it is necessary to suggest governments at all levels and relevant departments to take some measures for improvement of diet and nutrition of elderly apartments, and promote their health.

articleTitle: Study on the stability of HaiBo Capsules
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In this paper, the stability of HaiBo Capsules was investigated and its expiration period for clinical application was predicted. Based on the guiding principle of drug stability test, factors affecting the stability of HaiBo Capsules, such as bright light, high temperature and high humidity were observed under light of 4500 lx, at high temperature of 40D and in high humidity of RH 75-92.5%, exposing in air for six months. TLC was used for the measurement of betaine content in Haibo capsules. The results showed that the colour of content, the time limit for disintegration and other test indexes fitted the quality requirement. The accelerated test for the stability demonstrates that the package of the preparation can ensure the quality of the drugs. The preparation should avoid an environment with high temperature and humidity and be kept in a cool, dry and ventilated place, which can make it safe, stable and effective.

articleTitle: Autonomous learning mode of PE students under the network environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The rapid development of network technology led to a profound revolution in learning field. This paper combines with the characteristics of PE to explains the connotation of the autonomous learning under network environment bases on the theory of autonomous learning, to discusses and sums up the autonomous learning mode of PE students under the network environment at this basis.

articleTitle: Effects of platelets-derived growth factor receptor inhibitor on radiosensitivity of glioma cells
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In present study, we investigated the mechanism of AG1295, a platelets-derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) inhibitor, on radiosensitivity of the glioma cell line SHG-44. AG1295 induced a dose dependent cytotoxicity in the glioma cell line evidenced by MTT assay and the trypan blue dye exclusion method. Sensitization to ionizing radiation of SHG-44 was observed when pretreated with AG1295. Radiosensitization reached a peak at 24h after radiation. AG1295 markedly downregulated the expression of PDGFRa, but had little effect on the expression of PDGFRp. Flow cytometer assay revealed that AG1295 increased the G1 and G2 phases of the cell cycle, and Western blotting showed decreased cyclin B1 and cyclin D1 expression. AG1295 shows radiosensitizing effects on the SHG-44 glioma cells through a mechanism involving redistribution of the cell cycle by promoting cells to enter the radiation-sensitive G1 phase and G2 phase and inhibition of sublethal damage repair.

articleTitle: The study of correlative factors of nurses mental health, job burnout and personality in Jilin city
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Objective: To study situation of mental health, relationship mental health and job burnout and personality of nurses in the comprehensive hospitals in Jilin. Method: investigation and analysis of correlative factors of 317 clinical nurses by three scales: Symptom Checklist 90(SCL-90), Maslach Burnout Inventory (MBI), Eysenck Personality Questionnaire(EPQ) Result: There is statistical significance on factor of SCL-90, MBI as compared with the norm. There is significant correlation on factors of MBI, EPQ compared with factors of SCL-90. There is contribution to regression equation is the emotional exhaustion of MBI and the neuroticism and psychoticism of EPQ. Conclusion: The nurses have poor mental health level which is lower than that of the normal. The job burnout is obvious among nurses. There is significance correlation of mental health level compared with the job burnout and personality. The emotion affection and the personality factor are the deeper reason for poor mental health.

articleTitle: Research on the school-running characteristics and model of the sports university
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The school-running characteristics and model of running the sport universities and institutes are the fundamental problem to understand and practice the sports university. Discussing the unification of academicness and athleticness, establishing the school-running model with teaching, training and scientific research are very important for both promoting the development and enhancing the education quality and level of sports university. The characteristic and model of running the sport universities and institutes are the most essential and crucial problem. On the basis of the former researches, this paper, from the new angle of view, has tried to do the researches, taking the relationship between academicness and athleticness as a master line, to discuss the model of running sport universities and institutes which revolves the unification of academicness and athleticness, including the construction about the teaching, the training, and the research (abbreviation“ three-in-one connection”).

articleTitle: Research of Acanthopanax low health wine production
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In order to expand the development of health edible functions of Acanthopanax leaves, to meet people's demand for low care wine, Acanthopanax low alcohol wine was studied. Corn without Germ and Acanthopanax leaves are main materials, using double enzyme saccharification, low-temperature fermentation technology to produce low-alcohol wine. Saccharification process conditions was optimized by orthogonal experiment. The results showed that: Liquefaction time was 50 minutes, saccharification temperature was 55 □, glucoamylase dosage was 200U / g, pH5.0, saccharification time was 80 minutes, dosage of Acanthopanax leaves was 1.5 g / L. After Low-temperature fermentation, the alcohol concentration in an average was 4.5%. The appearance of wine was slightly yellow, clear and transparent. Because of a unique flavor and bitterness, no odor, and immune function, anti - fatigue, treatment of insomnia and so on, Acanthopanax low health wine has broad market and prospects.

articleTitle: Selenium assay on ordinary and selenium-rich rice in Jilin area and its effects on human body
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To investigate the content of selenium in ordinary and selenium-rich rice in Jilin area and understand its effects on human body. Selenium-rich rice were prepared using selenium-rich organic liquid fertilizer to spray during rice growing, then fed 6 groups Kunming mice using different doses of ordinary and selenium rice, 6 weeks later, blood DTNB direct method was used to detect the GSH-PX activity. Selenium content of both two kinds of rice using atomic fluorescence photometric. Selenium content in se-enriched rice is obviously higher than ordinary rice (P <; 0. 05), each dose group of selenium-rich rice compared with ordinary rice group, glutathione peroxidase (GSH - PX) activity enhanced obviously (P <; 0. 05), and the results give a suggestion that one adult needs intake selenium-rich rice daily 102.7 g, but needs ordinary rice 427.7 g. So selenium-rich rice utilization is benefit for the residents health and some disease prevention.

articleTitle: Study on the learning evaluation system of PE and health courses in universities
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Learning evaluation of physical education (PE) is a key link in the course of PE teaching, through which the teacher is able to complete the judgment of teaching mission while receiving feedback information as the basis of amelioration. In the meanwhile, the teacher, by this process of learning evaluation, is able to encourage, inspire and educate the students. The author commences with the presentation of the development of educational evaluation, in which the author probes into the topic deeply on the current study on learning evaluation of PE in universities both at home and abroad and then the author points out the problems existed in the system of learning evaluation of PE at home: it does not fully reflect the idea of “Health First” and restrict the PE educational development in universities. Therefore, reform should be imperative.

articleTitle: Effect of passive smoking on NO, GSH-pox, NOS, SOD, MDA in serum and lung homogenate of rats
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: This paper researched effect of passive smoking on growth rats. 30 male wistar rats were randomly devided control group(CG), low dose passive smoking group (LDG)and high dose passive smoking group(HDG), LDG and HDG breathed in smoke of three and six cigarettes respectively, twice every day, one time was one hour, altogether was 35 days. Body weight of LDG and HDG was significantly lower than CG (P <; 0.05). NO and MDA in HDG had significant difference to CG in serum and lung homogenate(P <; 0.05), GSH-pox in LDG was obviously lower than CG in serum and lung homogenate(P <; 0.05), NOS and SOD in HDG decreased significantly to LDG and CG in lung homogenate (P <; 0.05). Passive smoking may lead rats growing decreased, perhaps passive smoking made rats oxidation environment change.

articleTitle: Analysis of diabetic retinopathy vasculars image
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Image segmentation was adopted to process and analyze diabetic retinopathy vasculars so as to improve the efficiency and precision of clinical diagnosis. By means of selecting clinical fundus images as the research object and appling computer simulation software, retinal vessels were divided and extracted. After normal and pathological retinal image were processed and analysised, the vasculars were more fully revealed, and more precise than fundus images and fundus fluorescein angiography(FFA). Processing and analyzing of diabetic retinopathy vasculars based on image segmentation are more detail and clear, and precision has been significantly improved.

articleTitle: Effects of Arthrigia on adjuvant arthritis rats' serum TNF-α
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) is a systemic chronic autoimmune disease. To study the therapeutic mechanism of effects of Skullcap Brightviolet (SB), glucosamine/chondroitin (GC), and the combination of them (named Arthrigia) on RA. With the adjuvant arthritis (AA) rat models, we observed the protective effects of oral SB, GC and Arthrigia in different concentrations on AA in rats. We further examined the immunological mechanism of the combination of them by testing the rats' secretion of TNF-α. The results showed that Arthrigia inhibited the production and secretion of TNF-α factors in some extent, and its effects are more potent the single SB or GC. The present study provides the experimental evidences for Arthrigia for its further development, clinical prevention and treatment of RA.

articleTitle: Alice in wonderland syndrome as an initial manifestation of pediatric magraine: One case report and literature review
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Alice in wonderland syndrome is associated with migraine, epilepsy, infectious mononucleosis, Epstein-Barre viral infection and psychological disorders. It has rarely been reported in children. We report one case of pediatric migraine with onset as AIWS. A 13 years-old boy who experienced paroxysmal visual illusions for 6 years and headaches for 1 year. The child was previously misdiagnosed as pediatric schizophrenia. Symptoms of throbbing headache developed eventually. He had a family history of migraine Physical examination was unremarkable. Laboratory data such as brain CT, VEEG, routine test of cerebrospinal fluid, routine blood test, atypical lymphocyte in the peripheral blood smear and antibodies to EB virus were normal. TCD revealed the increased blood stream velocity The clinical diagnosis was made and topiramate was administrated. The symptoms of AIWS and headache resolved over half an year. Alertness to AIWS is helpful for making proper diagnosis and appropriate treatment of its associated disorders.

articleTitle: Effects of NaCl and pH on 2-hydroxypropyl-beta-cyclodextrin inclusion with oleanolic acid
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: This present work focused on the effects of NaCl and pH on 2-hydroxypropyl-beta-cyclodextrin (HPCD) inclusion with oleanolic acid by phase solubility analysis. The results indicated that the solubility of oleanolic acid could be increased by NaCl, so could the acidic pH and alkaline pH. Moreover, small effects of NaCl and pH on the solubility of oleanolic acid were observed at the low concentration of HPCD while large effects were observed at the high concentration of HPCD. It was suggest that hydrophobic interaction was the dominant driving forces for oleanolic acid encapsulated by HPCD in aqueous media.

articleTitle: Immunomodulatory effect of lectin from Musca domestic pupa on immunosuppressive mice: Effect of lectin on immunosuppressive mice
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The present study was conducted to elucidate the immunomodulatory effect of a lectin from Musca domestic pupa (MPL) in vivo. The effects of MPL (200, 400 and 800 μg/kg body wt.) on immune organ weight, mitogen-induced proliferation of spleen lymphocyte, phagocytosis activity of macrophages, NK cell activity, and the mRNA expression of immune factor in spleen like interleukin (IL) and interferon (IFN) were investigated in cyclophosphamide (CP) immunosuppressive mice. In comparison with that of immunosuppressive mice, the weight index of spleen and thymus were significantly increased (p<;0.05), the proliferation of spleen lymphocyte was enhanced, NK cell activity and phagocytosis activity of macrophages had been improved (p<;0.01) and the mRNA expression of IL-6, IL-12 and INF-γ in spleen were potentialized in a dose-dependent manner by MPL administration. These results demonstrated that MPL has a remarkable immunomodulatory effect on immunosuppressive mice, which suggested that MPL could be useful for further study as an immunomodulating agent.

articleTitle: Study of health education for university students in the new period
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Health education is an important part of school education. In this paper, we investigate the health problems of university students, the status of health education, students' knowledge of health and their attitudes. The problems existing in health education and their causes are analyzed, and the corresponding countermeasures and suggestions have been proposed to improve the health status of students.

articleTitle: Anti-nociceptive effects of DAACS water extract
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Direct reflux and TLC methods were used to isolate and identify de-aristolochic acid Aristolochia tuberosa C. F. Liang et S. M. Hwang (DAACS). Different doses of DAACS were administered intragastricly (i.g) and methods of hotplate, writhing, hot-bathing and tail-flick method were used to observe anti-nociceptive effects of DAACS; β-Endorphin (β-EP) and prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) contents of mice were detected with radioimmunoassay (RIA) to explore the anti-nociceptive mechanisms of DAACS. The results showed that DAACS (0.4, 0.8, 1.6 g·kg-1) could prolong mice' responsive latencies to hotplate significantly compared with those in the control group, delay writhing latencies of mice and reduce their writhing times, delay tail-flick latencies of mice, and reduce contents of β-EP in brain and PGE2 in liver tissue of formalin-treated mice significantly. DAACS would produce anti-nociceptive effects and its anti-nociceptive mechanism may be related to its effect on β-EP in brain and PGE2 in liver tissue of mice.

articleTitle: Expressions of matrix metalloproteinase-14 in the tissue of gastric carcinoma and their clinical significance
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To find out the expressions of matrix metalloproteinase-14 (MMP-14) in the tissue of gastric carcinoma, and to analyze their relationship to the clinicopathologic parameters of gastric carcinoma. collecting 80 surgical specimens of gastric carcinoma pathologically proved, detecting the expressions of MMP-14 by means of the immunohistochemical S-P and the data being processed using the statistical software SPSS17.0. the expression level of MMP-14 is statistically related to the infiltration depth of gastric carcinoma, Dukes stages, lymphatic metastasis, difference of cases (P<0.05), whereas the level is irrelevant to the patient's age, sex, tumor location, general classification, histological types and differentiation (P>0.05). MMP-14 is an important factor in the contraction and development of gastric carcinoma, which can be used as an index for the judgment of the invasion or metastasis of gastric carcinoma, and can also be a chief index for the prognosis of patients.

articleTitle: Leiomyosarcoma of the inferior vena cava: Curative resection and synchronous reconstruction of bilateral renal veins
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Leiomyosarcoma of the inferior vena cava (IVC) is a malignant tumor of mesenchymal origin. Surgical treatment should include complete resection of the malignant lesion with preservation of venous return. A 53-year-old woman, was referred to our hospital for recurrent upper abdominal discomfort. Computed tomography scan revealed a poorly-margined mass located between the pancreatic head and the right kidney, invading into inferior vena cava and bilateral renal veins. During surgical resection of the tumor, IVC and bilateral renal veins were clamped and the tumor was subsequently removed. The distal end of IVC was resected and venous prosthetic grafts were inserted into the proximal end and bilateral renal veins were reconstructed. Histological findings revealed leiomyosarcoma, originating from the IVC and infiltrating into bilateral renal veins. The patient has remained disease free after treatment. Though chemoradiotherapy may serve as adjuvant to surgical resection, complete surgical resection should also be recommended.

articleTitle: Feasibility of applying low contrast media volume in cervicocranial artery angiography with 256-slice CT
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Objective To evaluate the feasibility of applying low contrast medium volume in cervicocranial artery angiography with 256-slice CT. Materials and methods 30 patients undergoing cervicocranial artery CTA were enrolled into this study, and the patients were injected with low contrast medium volume (50 mL). Results the mean enhancement of the total segments was (292.50±80.70) HU. About 7 of 330 (97.88%) segments had enhancement ≥150HU which could be optimal for diagnosis. Conclusion Cervicocranial artery angiography with 256-slice CT can reduce contrast medium volume (33.3%).

articleTitle: Effects of different doses of X-ray on telomerase in human osteosarcoma cells (HOS cells)
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To investigate the effects of different doses of X-ray on the telomerase in human osteosarcoma (HOS) cells and to provide theoretical evidence for the clinical application of radiotherapy in osteosarcoma. Log phase HOS cells were radiated using 1, 2, 4 and 8 Gy doses of X-ray separately and cell survival was measured using MTT method, telomerase activity by ELISA, and telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) expression by immuno-histochemistry. Telomerase RNA was also quantitatively analyzed using RT-PCR. Cell apoptosis was positively correlated to X-ray doses and telomerase activity was enhanced greatly, as well as hTERT and telomerase RNA expression. Under the interference of X-ray, X-ray doses were negatively correlated to HOS cell survival and positively correlated to telomerase activity; HOS cell survival was negatively correlated to telomerase activity; hTERT, telomerase RNA and telomerase activity changed synchronically.

articleTitle: Practice of nursing students in elderly nutrition health education by human communication guiding pattern
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Objective: In this paper, the aim is to evaluate the result of elderly nutrition health education in the community carried out by nursing undergraduates using different human communication patterns and explore a method used for improve the ability of their self health education in practice. Method:245 Old people were selected to receive the instruction of nutrition health education by nursing undergraduates. Result: The result showed that effects of nutrition health education on both the elderly and the students were good. The human communication pattern can improve the result of nutrition health instruction efficiently on the elderly. During the practice, the students can be trained fully in nutrition health education, accumulate and integrate the knowledge of various subjects, deepen their understanding of the theory and get an opportunity to put it into practice. Conclusion: communication guiding pattern can not only improve their comprehensive quality but also play a good foundation for the clinical practice and the clinical work after their graduation in the future.

articleTitle: Study on the Trait Sport-confidence of the collegiate basketball athletes and its influence factors
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: As an important component of the athletes' comprehensive abilities; sport-confidence impacts on the athletic performance whether before or during the event. By means of documental data method, survey method, psychological measurement, and statistical method, the research had directed on the trait sport-confidence (SC-Trait) of collegiate basketball athletes who had participated in college basketball matches of shanghai, china and its influence factors. Collegiate basketball athletes (N=368) completed the Trait Sport-confidence Inventory and Influence Factors Questionnaire. Consistent with expectations, the elite group's SC-Trait level was significantly higher than that of the general group and there was no difference in the collegiate basketball athletes from different positions. The influence factors of collegiate basketball athletes' SC-Trait could be generalized as metal superiority factor, competitive ability factor, social example factor, tactical and strategic thought factor, value factor, economical condition factor, referee influence factor and culture level factor.

articleTitle: The effect of turmeric extract on rats acute myocardial ischemia model SOD
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Objective: To investigate the effect of Turmeric extract on rats acute myocardial ischemia model. Method: rats acute myocardial ischemia model, detect the SOD of blood plasma red blood cell and the content of SOD in tissue with SOD kit to reflect the level of SOD in tissue cells, to understand the produce rate of oxygen free radical in vivo and the degree of peroxidation action in lipid. Conclusion: The turmeric extract can increase the content of SOD in blood serum and myocardium tissue of rats acute myocardial ischemia model.

articleTitle: Effects of initial polytherapy in newly diagnosed West syndrome
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In order to explore the effects of initial polytherapy by combining ACTH followed by prednisone, topiramate, IVIG and vitamin B6 in newly diagnosed West syndrome. 51 children with West syndrome were included in our study. Forty-six patients became spasm-free through polytheray, two children effective and three ineffective. Statistical difference in time to spasm free was found between cryptogenetic patients and symptomatic cases. Of forty-six patients who became spasm free, hypsarrythmia was disappeared in 45 children except one with lissencephaly, normal 24h ambulatory EEG was got in 32 cases with seizure free, spike was found in 15 spasm free children, one case with lissencephaly with seizure free still had hypsarrythmia. Three cases relapsed during the follow-up. Our study demonstrates that initial polytherapy by combining ACTH, topiramate, vitamin B6 and IVIG in West syndrome is a worthwhile choice in clinic.

articleTitle: Betahistine is effective in combatting spasms in NMDA-inducing infantile spasms rat model
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Infantile spasms (IS) is an age-related epileptic disorder characterized by specific spasms, hypsarrhythmia and mental retardation. Most of IS patients can not get spasm free under the available treatment and prognosis is poor. It is crucial to develop new effective drugs the treatment of IS. Histamine H3 receptor antagonist seems to be effective in some epilepsy models. Betahistine is one of H3 antagonists. For this purpose, we tested the effecacy of betahistine in a NMDA-induced IS model. The results showed that betahistine prolonged the latencies to tail-flicking and emprothonus and decreased the incidence of stereotypic behaviors in IS rats. Betahistine has increased histamine content and H3 receptor expression in the brain in a dosage-dependent manner. Then, betahistine exerts it anti-spasms effect through increaing histamine content and H3 expression. It is promising for H3 antagonists use in IS in clinic to control spasms and improve the poor prognosis.

articleTitle: Effect of extracts from Mirablis jalapa root on small mice models of morphine dependence
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To observe effect of extracts from Root of Mirablis jalapa on Morphine Dependent mice. Mice of models and jasmine root extract were given morphine according a gradually increasing dose scheme, in which the morphine dose from 8 mg/ kg to 75 mg/kg during 2 days. Mirablis jalapa extract groups use administration by gavage in the second day; normal group, models group use physiological saline intragastrically, naloxone is injected by lumbar injection 30 minutes after the last morphine injection. This study successfully established models of morphine dependent mice. Extracts by sherwood oil, Chloroform can remedy withdrawal syndrome of female rats, have significant difference with models group (P<; 0.05), extracts by water, ether and sherwood oil can obviously improve withdrawal syndrome of male rats in comparison with models group (P<;0.05). Extracts from the Root of Mirablis jalapa can improve withdrawal syndrome, concrete mechanism need study futher.

articleTitle: Application of CD4+ CD25+ T regulatory cells in trachea allograft transplant model of mice to reject anti-graft response
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To study the role of CD4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> CD25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> Treg cells in anti-graft rejection response and potential value in application of lung transplatation, we established mice trachea allograft transplant model and sort CD4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> CD25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> Treg cells from mice spleen lymphocytes by MACS. FCM assays were done to analyze the ratio of marker protein, Foxp3, expression in CD4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> CD25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> Treg cells. Alveolar cells were used as a non-specific antigen to activate iDCs into mDCs, and cocultureed with CD4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> CD25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> Treg cells to activate Treg cells. The activated Treg cells were inject into mice with trachea allograft transplantation to reduce rejection response. The allografts were extracted and done pathological examination with H&E staining. The purity of CD4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> CD25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> Treg cells were over 80% and specifically express Foxp3, the organizational structure of implanted trachea showed that the tracheal structure was intact. Our research imply that CD4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> CD25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> Treg cells play an essential role in reducing rejection, and lay the foundation for reject anti-graft response in clinical application.

articleTitle: Clinical role of hWAPL in histologic diagnosis of cervical cancer and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia: Correlation with p16INK4a expression and HPV testing
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In this study, we examined the expression of hWAPL in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) I-III and cervical squamous cell carcinoma, and investigated clinical application value of hWAPL in diagnosis of cervical disease. 90 samples were collected, and two slides from each sample were immunostained using hWAPL and p16INK4a antibody. HPV-DNA testing was performed using the HC2 DNA test. The expression intensity of hWAPL in SCC group, CIN III group, CIN II group and CIN I group was obviously higher than that in normal cervix group, and the expression intensity in SCC group, CIN III group and CIN II group was higher than that in CIN I group. Based on ROC curves of hWAPL, when using ≥CIN I, ≥CIN II and ≥CIN III as cutoff for positive classification, area under the curve (AUC) was 0.815, 0.699, and 0.616, respectively. Therefore, hWAPL may be a promising candidate for diagnosis of low-grade CIN.

articleTitle: Optimization of allicin extraction by response surface method
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The extractive technique of allicin was investigated in this paper. The optimum extractive condition of allicin was determined through orthogonal design and response surface analysis as follows: the enzymatic hydrolysis time was 32.4min; temperature was 30; pH was 6.0; ratio of material to ethanol was 1:6.4; extracting time was 60min; extracting temperature 27.4; 95% ethanol. Under such condition, the extraction yield of allicin was 2.81<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>/<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00</sub> which was in good agreement with the response surface model.

articleTitle: Pharmacodynamical observation on anti-fatigue of fructose-1, 6-diphosphate sodium
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Through the biochemical detection (LA, CK, PFK, PK)of 40 testing athletes who taking quantitative FDP and placebo before anaerobictraining, 2hours after anaerobictraining and next morning, observe the actual results of anti-fatigue, the promotion of fatigue recovery and to further explore its mechanism. The result shows, taking FDP can promote glycolysis, quicken eliminate LA, promotion composing of hepatin; reduce CK evidently after anaerobictraining; taking exogenous FDP can also promote the resumption of the activity of PFK And at the same time, CK and LA of the Control group are significantly higher than the experimental group, that indicate taking exogenous FDP has obvious role in anti-fatigue after anaerobictraining.

articleTitle: Study on effect of α-Synuclein enhanced survival rate of rat primary cultured neuron
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To investigate the effect of α-Synuclein(α-Syn) on the survival rate of brain neurons. We isolated neurons from the neocortex of newborn rats were cultured and added α-Syn into the culture medium to observe the effect of the protein on the primary cultured neurons. In addition, the effect of different concentrations of α-Syn on the neuron growth was studied. The mean survival rate of primary cultured neurons treated with α-Syn was significantly highter than that of control neurons at 1h, 2h and 4h. The effect of α-Syn on increasing the primary cultured survival rate wasn't change with the increasing of α-Syn concentration and was reversed by anti-α-Syn monoclonal antibody. Western blot and Immunofluorescence staining assay showed α-Syn can enter into the neuron. We indicate that α-Syn can increase the survival rate of primary cultured neuron and it's a new physiological function of α-Syn.

articleTitle: Optimization of the conditions for Fructus Leonuri flavonoid extraction and research on its hypoglycemic effect
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Objective: To optimize the conditions for Fructus Leonuri flavonoid extraction and investigate the hypoglycemic effect of Fructus Leonuri flavonids on mice with diabetes mellitus. Methods: The conditions for Fructus Leonuri flavonoid extraction were optimized by analyzing extraction time, extraction temperature, ratio of solid and liquid, and ethanol concentration with orthogonal experiment. Effects of Fructus Leonuri flavonoids at different doses on diabetes mice were studied compared with the model group. Results: The best techniques conditions for Fructus Leonuri flavonoid extraction should be at the temperature of 60°C, in 60% ethanol concentration and in 1:20 ratio of solid and liquid; Fructus Leonuri flavonoids could produce a good hypoglycemic effect. Conclusion: Orthogonal experiment can be used to optimize the conditions for Fructus Leonuri flavonid extraction; Fructus Leonuri flavonoids can produce a significant good hypoglycemic effect. This study will play a good foundation for the further research on their pharmacological effects and biological activities of Fructus Leonuri flavonoids.

articleTitle: The research of the sports injury causes and countermeasures of cadets in physical training: By taking students of National University of Defense Technology as a study case
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The thesis uses the methodology of documentary file, questionnaire survey and survey to analyze the sports injury in physical training among 236 students of National University of Defense Technology and systematically states the mechanism of the injury formation from inside and outside to come up with the relative countermeasures with the view of reducing the injury risks and providing references to insure the physical training and competition.

articleTitle: The role of AcSDKP on inhibiting myofibroblast differentiation in rats with silicosis
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Myofibroblast differentiation, characterized by α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) expression, is a key process in organ fibrosis. Our recent studies have shown that AcSDKP has a anti-fibrotic effect in the lung of rats with silicosis. Here we explore the underlying effect of AcSDKP on myofibroblast differentiation during the anti-fibrotic process. SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> powders were instilled in trachea of rat to make the silicotic model, and caused 1) increased expressions of TGF-β, 2) escalated serum response factor (SRF) expression, 3) myofibroblast marked by o-SMA being detected in siliconic nodules, and 4) collagen deposition in lung. AcSDKP (both anti fibronic and prevention treatment) can inhibit these changes induced by silica significantly. AcSDKP could inhibit collagen synthesis throuth blocking myofibroblast differentiation in the lung of rats with silicosis, which is a new mechanism of its anti-silicotic effect.

articleTitle: Clinical analysis of the severity related factors of 602 cases of transient tachypnea of the newborn in preterm infants
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: The clinical manifestations of transient tachypnea of the newborn (TTN) in preterm infants are always different from the term infants because of the immature lungs, so retrospective study of clinical features and the severity related factors of disease can make sense for enhancing the understanding of TTN for pediatricians. 602 cases in preterm infants diagnosed with TTN at Neonatal Treatment Center of Jilin University for the last seven years were analyzed in this study, all the cases were divided into 2 groups according to gestational age (GA), including 256 cases of small GA preterm infants (<34 weeks' gestation) and 346 cases of near-term infants(34∼37 weeks' gestation). Each group was further divided into mild group and severe group depending on whether application of respiratory support (continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) and mechanical ventilation). We analyzed and compared the clinical features and the severity related factors of disease of infants between different gestational ages in preterm infants. The results showed the initial respiratory rate (RRin) was higher in severe group of TTN in small GA infants, while RRin and the mode of delivery were both statistically significant between mild and severe group in near-term infants. So this indicated elective caesarean section (CS) was the risk factor of severe condition in TTN of near-term infants, and RRin maybe the predictive factor of aggravation of the disease.

articleTitle: Effect of Tiscrazy Aroma Concord Parfum on psychophysiological coherence state
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: To investigate the effects of Tiscrazy Aroma Concord Parfum (TACP) on autonomous nervous system and job stress. 45 nurses (22±3 years old) were randomly allocated to three groups: a TACP group, a perfume control group, and a saline control group. The coherence scores of each participant in heart rate variability (HRV) determination were recorded were collected before and 20 min after the intervention at the first day of the trial. Saliva samples were collected before, 20 min after the intervention and at the 15th day. The levels of salivary chromogranin A (sCgA) were analyzed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. In the TACP group, the average scores increased significantly after the 20min usage(P<;0.05), and the average levels of sCgA at the 15th day were significantly lower than pre-test (P<;0.01). No significant changes were recorded in both perfume and saline control group. The TACP promotes a psychophysiological state conducive to stress reduction.

articleTitle: A study on marginal microleakage of five different restorative materials in vitro
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In order to select right restorative materials in clinic, we compared marginal microleakage of 5 different restorative materials in vitro. Fifty premolar teeth without dental carries which were extracted because of orthodontic treatment were assigned into five groups randomly. The box cavities were prepared on the buccal cervical surfaces of the premolars and then restored with five different restorative materials (Spectrum TPH, Dyract AP, Solitaire 2, FujiIIGC and GK amalgam). Then microleakages were assessed by measuring the extent of dye penetration along the restoration-tooth interface under stereomicroscope. The results showed the microleakage of amalgam was the most serious one of the five materials. The Solitaire 2 and Spectrum TPH had satisfied adhesive abilities to enamel in the occlusal margins, while Fuji_GC and Dyract AP had satisfied adhesive abilities to dentin in the gingival margins.

articleTitle: Energetics of ambulation with spring-loaded crutches
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Habitual users of underarm crutches may suffer severe shoulder and wrist pain. Our aim is to investigate the effect of using spring-loaded crutches on mechanical efficiency by comparing its performance with standard crutches through a biomechanical approach. In our experiments, seven male subjects were instructed to walk around a track on crutches for 5 minutes under 4 controlled conditions. The externally-loaded and segmental work involved with the motions was computed based on ground reaction forces and centre of motion trajectories. Simultaneously, portable gas analysis machinery was used to collect the metabolic parameters of subjects to work out mechanical efficiency, the ratio of mechanical to metabolic work. It was found that the mechanical efficiency was significantly higher when subjects walked with spring-loaded crutches than when they walked with standard crutches.

articleTitle: Isolation and identification of probiotic lactic acid bacteria from pickles
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: For the purpose of obtaining probiotic starters to produce functional pickles, 59 strains were isolated from 15 samples of brine And two promising strains labled A18 and B17 were screened out according to their ability of producing organic acid and survival in the models environment of stomach and small intestine. The strians were identified and analyzed by morphology properties of the colony and the cell together with the sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene, data indicated that both strains were Lactobacillus plantarum.

articleTitle: Construction of expression vector for lvgA/ctxB-EGFP fusion gene and study on its immunogenicity
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Legionella pneumophila is an intracellular bacteria, and its successful parasitism in host cells involves two reciprocal phases: transmission and intracellular replication. In this study, we try to construct expression vectors of pcDNA3.1 (+)-lvgA/ctxB-EGFP fused gene and to investigate its transient expressions in NIH3T3 cells. Then preliminary analysis the immunogenicity of lvgA/ctxB fusion gene. The recombinant plamids pcDNA3.1(+)-EGFP, pcDNA3.1(+)-lvgA-EGFP, pcDNA3.1 (+)-ctxB-EGFP, pcDNA3.1(+)-lvgA/ ctxB-EGFP were transfected into NIH3T3 cells respectively with Lipofection method; Transient products were detected by immunofluorescence assay (IFA) and Western blotting. Study on there immunogenicity through the detection of cytokines in mice immunization. Mice were immunized intramusculary with different plasmids DNA as vaccines for immunization by detection the production of IFN-γ, IL-8. It was found that there was green fluorescence on the cells membrane and inside the cells and showed that NIH3T3 cells were transfected by fused expression vectors successfully, the production of IFN-γ, IL-8 by blood of mice immunized with fused genes all higher than pcDNA3.1(+) group and the production of pcDNA3.1(+)-lvgA/ctxB immunized was the most highest. The fused expression vectors were successfully constructed and transfected in NIH3T3 and induced specific immune responses in mice, the group immunized by the pcDNA3.1(+)-lvgA/ctxB was most obviously, which provide the basis for the research on DNA vaccine of Legionella pneumophila.

articleTitle: Investigation of the effects of the retention groove location and dimensions of threaded glass fiber post on biomechanical responses of the restorative system
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Effects of retention groove location and dimensions of threaded glass fiber post on the maximum retention force of the restorative system and the maximum equivalent stress in the root were numerically investigated. Results show that the retention groove can effectively enhance retention ability and reduce the stress in the root. And the maximum retention force of the restorative system can be increased by 5% and the maximum equivalent stress in the root decreased by 3% compared with corresponding maximum values if location and dimensions vary in the range studied here. The maximum retention force is more sensitive to retention groove distance while the maximum equivalent stress in the root is more seriously affected by retention groove depth.

articleTitle: Construction of prokaryotic vector of Timp-3
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: Purposes: constructing prokaryotic vector of Timp3 (tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase-3). Methords: Total RNA of human placenta tissues were prepared, and the cDNA encoding Timp3 was got via RT-PCR. The gene was constructed into pMD18-T vector using the restriction enzyme of BamHI and XbaI. Results: By agrose gel electrophoresis and DNA sequencing, Timp3 gene was introduced into pMD18-T successly.

articleTitle: Study on the establishment of the healthcare information framework
publicationTitle: Proceedings 2011 International Conference on Human Health and Biomedical Engineering
abstract: In order to better express, organize and store all kinds of medical and health information, achieve information exchange and sharing, promote information integration and fusion, form the decision support of various types intelligence and knowledge, meet the needs of the clinical, research and management for comprehensive utilization of various information, ultimately improve the medical and health service quality, we study and establish a comprehensive framework for medical and health information based on the characteristics of health care and medical health information.
